b05a69fa219b8940: TOKYO: When Japan's "symbol of affordability" Uniqlo decided to increase the price of its basic socks last month, it sparked a backlash before the clothing titan made an immediate U-turn.

That came after Italian-style family restaurant chain Saizeriya issued an almost grovelling apology as it decided to add 20 yen (US$0.13) to the price of its trademark Milanese Doria, lamenting its "lack of effort."

The very public angst – including in one of the world's most recognisable clothing brands – highlights the struggles Japanese firms face as they battle rising costs in a country where decades of deflation have nurtured a consumer class averse to higher prices.
The Bank of Japan last month declared its two-percent inflation target had been met, after 13 years of ultra-loose monetary policy.

Measures unveiled in 2013 by then-prime minister Shinzo Abe – and continued by successive governments – were supposed to end a spiral of deflation that had plagued Japan for decades since the mid-1990s.
However, it wasn't until 2022 – when the Ukraine war triggered a global energy shock – that inflation started flickering back to life in resource-poor Japan.

Then the US-Israel war on Iran saw Tehran choke off the strategic Strait of Hormuz, slashing crude exports from the Middle East and impacting global supply chains, in turn sending company costs soaring.
'SORRY FOR OUR CUSTOMERS'
While firms in most countries have been able to lift prices accordingly – albeit to expected anger – those in Japan have to battle an inherent view that hikes are taboo.
Businesses big and small have found themselves hard-pressed to plough ahead with drastic price hikes to avoid alienating customers.
Decisive increases can be more of a risk for smaller, countryside businesses whose survival often hinges on loyal patronage by regular clients.
Sachi, 68, a ramen shop owner in western Japan's Okayama region, has been holding off on raising prices despite snowballing costs.

"When I imagine myself suddenly announcing a 200-yen hike, for example, I cannot help but feel guilty and sorry for our customers who have supported us for years," Sachi, who only gave her first name, told AFP during a recent trip to Tokyo.
"So my thinking is, 'I would rather persevere myself'. I think lots of tiny businesses are like that, especially in rural areas."
Uniqlo's decision to row back on its sock price hike came as it sought to protect its status as a paragon of affordability portrayed in local media.
Saizeriya, whose price increases went far beyond Doria to cover almost all menu items, issued a statement some saw as self-flagellating.
The company's president even vowed at a news conference to "look for any excuses to lower prices again", to the amazement of social media users.
Still, the chain kept other items such as wine – a stunningly cheap 100 yen per glass – unchanged because "we want it to be enjoyed casually", its public relations office told AFP.
'INSANELY HIGH'

Soaring grocery bills have left Japanese households less room to spend on other purchases, from dining out to clothing, even as these businesses grapple with rising labour and material costs of their own.
This is despite recent labour ministry statistics showing real wages in Japan have increased year-on-year for eight consecutive months.
"Food prices are getting insanely high, so I have to increasingly rely on stuff imported from overseas, because homegrown products cost me more," Tokyo office worker Kazuhiko Sato told AFP.
"I'm also eating out less," he said.
To make matters worse, the Bank of Japan has embarked on a period of interest rate increases to battle inflation, with borrowing costs at a more than 30-year high and likely to go up again.
Tsutomu Watanabe, the professor at the University of Tokyo's graduate school of economics, said: "Pay raises are still largely insufficient and not benefiting everyone."
A similar or even higher rate of inflation permeates other Group of Seven economies, but "wage hikes there have been decent enough to keep spending from weakening", he told AFP.
Therein lies a key difference from Japan, which essentially remains "a convalescent trying to recover from decades of deflation", the economist said.
"The pricing power of companies is still pretty much dictated by consumers" in Japan, he said.
He thinks it will be "another three to four years" before Japanese consumers undergo a mentality shift to accept chronic inflation as the natural result of steep wage increases.
"After 30 years of deflation, transitioning to a different regime inevitably takes some time," he said.

41842984619f5d9e: ASUNCION (Paraguay), Nov 8 — Paraguayan prosecutors charged ex-president Santiago Pena and took him into custody Saturday over a banking crisis that saw millions of people cut off from their money, sparking major protests.
Pena, Paraguay’s youngest-ever president at 47, was removed from office by the Senate on Friday, just three days after the collapse of a leading bank with which he had business links.
He had offered to resign but lawmakers impeached him instead, stripping him of the immunity he would have enjoyed had he stepped down.
In a fast-moving sequence of events, Pena was brought before prosecutors on Saturday and charged with “breach of trust and mismanagement for personal gain.”
Ueno Bank was a popular online bank that held accounts for nearly half of Paraguay’s 6.5 million people, plus more than US$800 million in government funds.
Its collapse rocked this small, normally stable country, leading to street protests.
Pena, who came to power in 2023, owned shares in the bank’s holding company, Ueno Holding, until he sold them last year.

He is accused of using his influence as president to steer millions in government deposits to Ueno Bank and of hiding or downplaying its financial woes, even though he was warned about questionable loans and solvency issues.
Pena is also accused of a conflict of interest for naming former Ueno Bank director Carlos Carvallo to run Paraguay’s Central Bank.
Pena’s lawyer Ricardo Preda denied the charges against his client and said that in Paraguay, it is not the president but rather a minister who decides where government money is deposited.

After a hearing with Pena on Saturday, Judge Hernan Otazu told reporters he had ordered the former president taken into pre-trial custody and held at the same Asuncion facility where he was taken after his removal from office on Friday.
The judge froze the assets of Pena and Carvallo, who faces the same charges as the former president, plus one of falsifying government documents.
Pena declined to make a statement during the hearing, Otazu said.
The Central Bank said it has started paying out money to Ueno Bank customers caught up in the collapse and that more than 50 per cent have recovered their funds.
Giovanni Catolinom, 40, was not one of them. He trembled as he told AFP that funds from his new travel agency — around US$16,000 — were still trapped in the bank.
“I lost 16 years of work,” he said, crying.
Pena was replaced by Vice President Pedro Alliana, who promised not to abandon the depositors, including pensioners, affected by Ueno’s demise.
On the streets of Asuncion there was rejoicing over Pena’s ouster.
But news that Alliana, who is from the same right-wing Colorado Party as Pena, would take over angered some demonstrators.
“He’s from the same team, he knew about it (the trouble at Ueno),” Edson Vazquez told AFP.
US ally
The collapse of Ueno rocked usually stable Paraguay.
Thousands of people took to the streets furiously demanding their money back after the Central Bank took control of Ueno, citing fears for its solvency.
Pena’s removal was a further blow for US President Donald Trump’s network of allies in South America.
Trump’s favourite for Brazilian president, Flavio Bolsonaro, was defeated by left-wing incumbent Lula Inacio Lula da Silva last month.
Alliana will serve out the remainder of Pena’s term, which ends in 2028. — AFP

bf2b84d03653483f: KUALA LUMPUR: Former world No. 14 Ng Tze Yong could end an absence of more than 18 months from international badminton at the Algeria International next month.

The 26-year-old Malaysian is listed as 25th in men's singles qualifying for the Dec 2-5 tournament in El Biar, where he would make his first appearance on the international circuit as an independent player.
Tze Yong took part in an exhibition at Acacia Ridge in Brisbane on Saturday, with organisers Smashminton Brisbane posting highlights from the event they hosted with Klutch Badminton Academy.

He had also entered the South Australia International in Adelaide and the Melbourne International, scheduled for successive weeks this month, but both official entry lists show his name was removed on Oct 1.
His entry for Algeria was still active on Sunday, offering the 2022 Commonwealth Games silver medallist a chance to play his first international tournament since last year's Malaysia Masters.
His singles silver in Birmingham came in the Commonwealth Games campaign, where he helped Malaysia win the mixed team gold.
Tze Yong was chasing a place at the Paris Olympics when his injury troubles began on Jan 10, 2024, less than two months after he reached a career-high world No. 14.
Trailing Japan's Koki Watanabe 12-8 in the opening game of their Malaysia Open first-round match in Bukit Jalil, Tze Yong hurt his back attempting a jump smash and had to retire.
A back muscle tear forced him to miss the India Open, Indonesia Masters and Thailand Masters before he returned at the Badminton Asia Team Championships in Shah Alam in February.
He suffered a separate back injury at the team event and underwent operations in February and April, ending his bid for Paris and keeping him out for the rest of 2024.
It was April last year before Tze Yong played another international tournament, returning at the Asian Championships in Ningbo after more than a year on the sidelines.

He played the Taiwan and Thailand Opens before his comeback ended at his fourth tournament, when he injured his right knee against Hong Kong's Ng Ka Long in the first round of the Malaysia Masters in May.
Tze Yong underwent surgery for a torn anterior cruciate ligament at the Aspetar Orthopaedic and Sports Medicine Hospital in Doha in July and began his rehabilitation in Qatar.
By January this year, he had resumed light court work, but in June he put his training intensity at only 40 to 50 per cent.
By then he had fallen out of the world rankings, and on June 30 he left the BA of Malaysia by mutual agreement to pursue his career as an independent player.
Tze Yong joined Felet and began training on July 1 at Next Level Badminton Academy in Petaling Jaya under former international Soong Joo Ven, his former teammate in the national squad.
In Algeria, Tze Yong would have to qualify for a place in the main draw, with Nov 23 the deadline to withdraw without penalty.
401442f3a144ed52: TEHERAN: Two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday, according to state news agency IRNA.
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Teheran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

"Two oil tankers violating regulations – one in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the strait – caught fire and are currently engulfed in intense flames after striking naval mines while attempting to cross through unauthorised routes," the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said in a statement.

"The two tankers had reportedly committed multiple violations, including switching off their navigation and positioning systems, as they attempted to transit through an unauthorised route," the statement added.
The Guards did not specify the name or nationality of the tankers.
Teheran has made multiple announcements in recent weeks saying that ships have caught fire in the Hormuz strait.

US Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.
The IRNA separately reported late on Saturday that sounds of explosions were heard in parts of the country.
"Sounds resembling explosions were heard in Qeshm, Sirik, Jask, and Bandar Abbas. The cause of the sounds remains unknown," the news agency wrote on Telegram.
Officials confirmed an "impact" in the port city of Jask, the IRNA said.
US President Donald Trump previously talked up the possibility of resuming heavy strikes on Iran but has since walked back from the idea.
Nevertheless, the US military has conducted occasional limited strikes.--AFP

fffd7cf764a6d455: MELAKA: PKR has cautioned its 10 candidates contesting the Melaka election against behaving like 'orang besar' (VIPs) or becoming overconfident, assuming they have an advantage just because they represent the party led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

Acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said the party wanted to approach the election with humility, even positioning itself as an underdog rather than relying on its status as a party in the federal government.
He said representing Anwar's party also came with expectations and pressure to secure electoral victories, but PKR viewed these as challenges rather than advantages.

"That pressure is always there, but we turn it into a challenge. If we look at the bigger picture, we believe the strategies and approaches we adopt in this election could help us prepare for the next general election.
"Others may say this is the prime minister's party, a party with many ministers and one that controls the country's administration, but we are not approaching the election that way.
"We should not assume that we are different just because Pakatan Harapan has the prime minister and is now in government.
"We are no different from others. We remain mindful and do not become arrogant," he said during Bicara PRN Melaka podcast here.
PH, a coalition led by PKR, is fielding 24 candidates in the election.
Apart from PKR, which is contesting 10 seats, its two other component parties, DAP and Amanah, are fielding seven candidates each.
Adam Adli, who is also PKR communications director, said the party did not want PH candidates to become overconfident, as this could lead to complacency.
He acknowledged that voter demographics might appear unfavourable to PH based on projections, but said voting patterns in Melaka could not be determined solely by theoretical evaluation.
"We are doing our best. At this point, we can see a light at the end of the tunnel, with some potential emerging in several constituencies we are contesting.

"However, we must ensure that we do not make mistakes and that we redouble our efforts. Even if PH fails to meet its target, the work we have put in during this election will not necessarily go to waste, as it can be continued in the next general election," he said.
He said that despite being part of the unity government, PH remained realistic in fielding candidates in only 24 seats, taking into account the strength of its election machinery.
"People look at PH as though we are already wealthy, when our strength remains much the same as before. There may be more people supporting us, but that does not mean we can do whatever we want.
"We cannot simply decide to contest all 28 seats without careful consideration. We have to properly assess our strength before making such decisions," he said.
Meanwhile, Adam Adli acknowledged that Bersama's participation in the Melaka election, with 16 candidates, had some impact on PH, but described it as a minor disruption rather than a major setback.
He said that while PKR would not underestimate the capabilities of Bersama, led by Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, he remained confident that PH was strong enough to face the challenge.

"Of course there is an impact. We cannot say otherwise. We will not underestimate them, but suffice to say that PH remains a significant force. We may be affected, but not to the extent of being seriously weakened," he said.

573c95feaea78b5d: PUTRAJAYA: Motorcyclists are raising the alarm over a stretch of road linking the Maju Expressway to Putrajaya after several riders claimed to have crashed at the same spot, particularly during rainy weather.
The issue has gained traction on social media, with a video showing a motorcyclist skidding on the wet road drawing more than 256,000 views on Threads.

The video, posted by Threads user harithhamdan on Nov 6, shows a motorcyclist losing balance and falling while about to merge lanes on a wet stretch of the Putrajaya ring road after the Maju Expressway, with the caption: "Be careful riding in the rain."
View on Threads
Threads user shaf_ajer said he and his wife fell there in early December last year.
"I broke my shoulder, my wife suffered a concussion that caused memory loss," he wrote.
User nurnaqiahmahadzir said she and her husband crashed at the spot on Oct 17 while it was raining, less than three weeks before the video was posted.
"There is a black line on the road that makes it slippery and road users do not notice they are about to fall," she wrote.
Responding to her, harithhamdan said: "It's true, there is an uneven surface when merging with the main road there."
User hanzwindscreen claimed motorcycles had fallen at the location many times before and that he had nearly fallen there himself.
"I myself nearly fell there because of a pothole before this. Then they resurfaced it.
"The problem is the resurfacing used a slippery surface like black paint," he wrote.
User aminharis_ also pointed to the same black line on the road surface.
"There is a black line (not tar) in that area of the road. Whenever it rains, that black line is automatically slippery even if you ride slowly," he wrote.
Putrajaya Member of Parliament Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin has also responded to the issue on Threads.
"I will look into it and follow up with the relevant parties," Radzi replied.
In a similar incident in September, a viral video showed several motorcyclists falling on a rain-soaked green-painted stretch of the Federal Highway motorcycle lane near Subang.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi later said the lane would be resurfaced and fitted with a 40kph speed limit sign.
The New Straits Times has reached out to the Public Works Department and Maju Expressway Sdn Bhd for comment.

Rauf berkata, kerjasama BN dan PN menerusi Muafakat Melaka mampu membawa dimensi baharu dalam politik negeri dengan menyatukan kekuatan daripada pelbagai latar belakang demi kestabilan.
Beliau yakin calon PN, Albert Kok yang juga anak jati Kesidang mampu memberikan perkhidmatan terbaik kepada penduduk, jika menang pada 14 Nov ini.

"Saya mengarahkan semua jentera Umno dan BN, termasuk MCA dan MIC, bergerak bersama dengan PN bagi memastikan Kesidang ini kembali kepada Muafakat Melaka yang akan diterjemahkan pada 14 Nov ini," katanya yang berpuas hati dengan komitmen jentera dua gabungan membuktikan kesepakatan menerusi Muafakat Melaka.

Pada PRN Melaka 2021, calon Pakatan Harapan (PH) daripada DAP, Seah Shoo Chin mempertahankan kerusi Kesidang dengan 14,769 undi, menewaskan calon BN, Leong Hui Ying (4,532 undi) dan calon PN, Patrick Ng Chin Kae (3,124 undi).
Kok akan bertembung Seah yang dalam misi mempertahankan kerusi itu serta calon Parti Bersama Malaysia, Dr Bryan Kek pada Sabtu ini.
6afd7974224f2537: LONDON: A British monarch has only ever made one state visit to China: Queen Elizabeth II four decades ago. King Charles III would consider undertaking the second, according to an aide.
"If the government said, 'Will the king go to China?' I think, you know we think about it very carefully," a senior palace aide told reporters this week.
The late queen, Charles's mother, visited China with her husband Prince Philip in October 1986.
The trip included stops in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou, according to reports at the time.
It came two years after the signing of the Sino-British Joint Declaration setting out the terms for the return of Hong Kong, which improved relations between the two countries.
"This is the 40th anniversary of the last state visit," noted the aide, speaking at the end of the king's nine-day tour of the Caribbean.
Charles's trip was dominated by the thorny subject of slavery reparations. He called the transatlantic slave trade a "monstrous injustice" as the UK government mulls an apology.
"I think what we're seeing is a very clear pattern emerging of the government asking the king to head into quite politically charged situations, quite challenging situations," said the aide.
The king, who is politically neutral, "relishes" the "tough parts" of his role and can be a "great secret weapon" for the government, the aide added.

"Whether that's leading on the environment, whether it's renewing and refreshing and reinvigorating relationships with nations where there have been some complex political issues at play, that is what he lives and breathes for," they said.
Charles, who is nearly 78 and still being treated for an undisclosed cancer, was widely praised for his state visit to the US and delicate handling of US president Donald Trump earlier this year.

Relations between London and Beijing have been strained for years, fuelled in part by tensions over the political situation in former British colony Hong Kong, criticism of Beijing's human rights record and spying allegations.
But UK prime minister Andy Burnham is now pursuing the same policy of cautious rapprochement started by his predecessor Keir Starmer, who visited Beijing in January.
"China is a hugely important country. It's a very complex country. It would pose you know a lot of complexity in putting a program together," Charles's aide said.
As then prince of Wales, Charles oversaw Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule as Britain's most senior representative at the 1997 handover alongside China's then president Jiang Zemin.
Asked whether Burnham would be asking the king to visit China, his spokesman told AFP that questions about the monarch's travel was "one for the palace".
f7590b76cd480063: LOS ANGELES: Jalen Brunson scored 31 points to propel the NBA champion New York Knicks to a convincing 109-97 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Saturday in a rematch of last season's Eastern Conference finals.

Brunson scored 18 points in the second quarter as the Knicks broke open a close game in Cleveland, where the Cavs were coming off an impressive win over LeBron James and the Eastern Conference-leading Philadelphia 76ers on Friday.
The NBA Finals Most Valuable Player added six rebounds and nine assists.
Karl-Anthony Towns had 29 points with 13 rebounds and two steals for the Knicks, who notched their fifth win in six games after starting the season 0-3.
Donovan Mitchell scored 37 points to lead the Cavs, but Cleveland felt the absence of center Jarrett Allen and when Brunson took over in the second period they couldn't respond.
The Knicks pushed the lead to as many as 19 points. They connected on just 42.7% of their shots from the field but came up with 26 second-chance points off 16 offensive rebounds.

"Ugly game, but just a good win by our guys," Knicks coach Mike Brown said. "We did enough to get it done in some way, shape or form. Anytime you can get a win, especially with us starting out 0-3, we'll take it to see if we can build a little positive equity at this point in the season."
In San Francisco, Stephen Curry scored 19 of his 41 points in the fourth quarter and overtime to help the Golden State Warriors escape with a 126-119 victory over the Orlando Magic.
Golden State led by as many as 16, but with the help of 19 Warriors turnovers the Magic clawed back and a frantic fourth quarter saw Orlando's Jamal Cain tie it with 1.5 seconds left in regulation.

Curry converted a three-point play with 1:38 left in the extra session that put Golden State up by two and added a layup with less than a minute remaining to help the Warriors hang on for a seventh straight win.
Curry, 38, posted his second 40-point game this season and passed LeBron James for most 40-point games after the age of 35 with his 16th.
- Mexico City Game -
Saturday's seven-game slate started with the NBA's latest foray south of the border for its 16th regular-season contest in Mexico.
Three-time MVP Nikola Jokic scored 19 points and grabbed 13 rebounds to help the Denver Nuggets hold off the Indiana Pacers' second-half surge and emerge with a 114-102 triumph.
Jokic added eight assists, coming up just shy of a triple-double.

Cameron Johnson added 18 points and Jamal Murray chipped in 16 for the Nuggets, who saw a 27-point lead sliced to seven midway through the fourth quarter but held on for the victory before a sellout crowd of more than 20,000 at Mexico City's Arena CDMX.
"It was a good crowd," Jokic said. "The energy was there the whole game. I didn't know who they were cheering for, for us or for them, but the energy was there."
Indiana's Pascal Siakam led all scorers with 23 points, but the Pacers trailed by as many as 27 in the first half.
They hit back with a 37-point third quarter and pulled within 102-95 on a Jarace Walker running basket with 7:27 remaining.
The Nuggets responded with a quick basket from Spencer Jones and a thunderous Aaron Gordon dunk as they kept the Pacers at bay.
In Oklahoma City, the Thunder rolled to a 114-75 victory over Washington, holding the Wizards to the lowest points total in the NBA this season.
Two-time reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led Oklahoma City with 30 points and nine assists.

Jared McCain added 19 off the bench and rookie Aday Mara chipped in 18 points, eight rebounds, and three assists as the Thunder continued to thrive despite the injury absences of Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. - AFP

c130a3d683691169: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Attorney-General (A-G) Tan Sri Mohamed Apandi Ali said the Pardons Board's decision granting Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, was clear and unambiguous.
He said the board's decision must be implemented in accordance with what had been decided, without any deviation.
He said Article 42(9) of the Federal Constitution clearly stipulated that, before giving its advice on any matter, the Pardons Board must consider any written opinion submitted by the A-G.
"Certainly, the AG's opinion for the purpose of the pardon must have been in favour of granting the pardon.
"So, why does the AG now appear to be changing his position on the pardon? This situation is highly unreasonable," he said in a statement.
Apandi said he agreed with the decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, that there was no ambiguity in the Pardons Board's decision.

In a statement yesterday, Istana Negara said any arguments disputing the conditional pardon order granted to the former prime minister could be construed as an act of defying the decree of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
It said all conditions stipulated in the conditional pardon order had been fulfilled and its implementation should not give rise to confusion or prolonged uncertainty.
Meanwhile, Apandi said Article 4 of the Federal Constitution established the Constitution as the supreme law of the country, while Article 5 provided for the right to personal liberty.
"The law applies to everyone. Refer to Article 8 (equality) of the Federal Constitution," he said.
Article 8(1), among other things, states that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to equal protection of the law.

The Prime Minister's Department's Legal Affairs Division, in a statement last September, said the Yang di-Pertuan Agong had consented to grant Najib a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, provided he paid a RM50 million fine.

On Friday, Najib's lawyer, Muhammad Farhan Shafee, confirmed that the former Pekan member of parliament had settled the RM50 million fine imposed on him in the SRC International Sdn Bhd fund misappropriation case at the High Court Registry here.
In July 2020, Najib, who was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds, was fined RM210 million and sentenced to 12 years in prison.
The sentence was upheld by the Federal Court in August 2022.

However, on Feb 2, 2024, the Pardons Board Secretariat announced that Najib had been granted a 50 per cent reduction in his prison sentence, from 12 years to six years, while his fine was reduced from RM210 million to RM50 million.
3dc090ea1b1afe52: GEORGE TOWN: Penang residents have been advised to stay vigilant as thunderstorms and frequent rain are forecast across the state until Tuesday.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) weather outlook indicated a trend of wet weather over the three-day period, particularly during afternoons and evenings.
Today, rain is anticipated in several areas in the morning, followed by thunderstorms across most parts in the afternoon and rain continuing into the night.
Tomorrow, wetter conditions are expected with morning showers across most areas, widespread thunderstorms across the state in the afternoon and continuous rain at night.

On Tuesday, morning showers are expected along coastal stretches, with weather conditions tapering off slightly later in the day, though localised thunderstorms and rain remain forecast for the afternoon and evening.
MetMalaysia said that no Continuous Rain Warning (Alert category) has been issued for Penang so far, as current warnings remain focused on selected districts in Kelantan, Terengganu and Sabah.
Following the forecast, the Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations division urged the public to stay abreast of official weather advisories.
"Residents, especially those living in low-lying and flash flood-prone areas, are advised to avoid high-risk routes during severe weather.
"Members of the public requiring emergency assistance or evacuation are urged to call the 24-hour 999 hotline immediately," it said.
The department said its personnel are on full alert to handle any disaster response throughout the northeast monsoon period to safeguard lives and property.
9a61ac9d8b5eeb3d: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — British actor Riz Ahmed has said he loved Malaysian food so much while filming in Penang that he gained weight during the shoot and had to get his trousers refitted.
The Emmy-winning actor made the admission during an appearance on the Dish from Waitrose podcast, hosted by broadcaster Nick Grimshaw and Michelin-starred chef Angela Hartnett.
Host Grimshaw asked, “You’re a big fan of Malaysian food as well?”

Ahmed said, “What I like about Malaysian food is, it’s Indonesian food, Indian food, obviously its own kind of Malay flavours and Chinese food, all kind of thrown together. So you get this amazing mix of stuff.
“Obviously they do the rotis, they do rotis with rendang, with not nasi goreng, but with a twist.”
He said, “I gotta tell you, I put on so much weight there they had to refit my costume... Literally they had to redo my trousers, they had to do the whole thing.”
However, he said he had "no regrets" about the experience.
Ahmed, 43, is a British-Pakistani actor and rapper who won an Emmy for his role in The Night Of and received an Oscar nomination for Sound of Metal.
During the podcast, the actor discussed his time in Malaysia while working on the Netflix film The Big Fix, a crime thriller starring Mark Wahlberg and directed by Baltasar Kormákur.
The film, inspired by a true story, follows a former Interpol officer who uncovers an international football match-fixing operation.
Dish from Waitrose has been running since 2022 and has featured guests including Gordon Ramsay, Dua Lipa and Benedict Cumberbatch.
The podcast pairs celebrity guests with food conversations and cooking segments.
b6a35d82531f89a6: SEBERANG PERAI, Nov 8 — Healthcare workers were seen holding umbrellas indoors at Seberang Jaya Hospital last night as rainwater poured through leaking ceilings and spread across flooded corridors, in video footage that has since gone viral.
Penang Health director Dr Zulhizzam Abdullah confirmed that heavy rain and strong winds sent water seeping into several parts of the hospital, the New Straits Times reported today.
“Most affected areas involved the hospital’s older building blocks, though several newer buildings were also impacted,” he was quoted as saying.
“This was an unforeseen incident due to torrential rain, gale-force winds and massive runoff.
“However, no patients were affected, and no adverse incidents were reported,” he added.
Dr Zulhizzam said the hospital’s engineering and maintenance management department had moved to address the situation immediately.
Malaysia is currently in the north-east monsoon season, which is expected to continue until March next year.
fa69e71d333aa9c4: MELAKA: Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh is optimistic that the cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the Melaka election could spring a surprise in Pakatan Harapan's stronghold of Kesidang.

The Melaka BN chairman said the consolidation of support among members and supporters of the two coalitions under the Muafakat Melaka spirit signalled a major shift in the country's political landscape.
"If we reclaim Kesidang under Muafakat Melaka, as I said earlier, it will mark a significant change.

"If we succeed in winning the Kesidang seat, it will send a strong signal that the political movement in Melaka will pave the way for a better journey towards Putrajaya," he told reporters after visiting the Kesidang seat operations room in Malim Jaya here today.
Also present was PN candidate for Kesidang Albert Kok, who is also Kota Melaka Wawasan division deputy chief.

Ab Rauf, who is also caretaker Melaka chief minister, added that he was satisfied with the campaign efforts of both coalitions' machinery after a week on the campaign trail, saying they had demonstrated their commitment to the Muafakat Melaka spirit.
"I can see that the campaign machinery at all levels, from both PN and BN, has been working together and demonstrating that this cooperation is solid. I am very satisfied.
"As I have said before, the people of Melaka are like those observing Ramadan. They eagerly await the moment to break their fast.
"Just wait until the time comes. When the Maghrib azan is sounded, we will see how they (the voters) cast their votes," he said.
Kok is involved in a three-cornered contest as BN and PN seek to wrest Kesidang from incumbent DAP assemblyman Allex Seah Shoo Chin and Bersama candidate Dr Bryan Kek Kit Hun.
In the 2021 state election, Seah won the seat with a majority of 10,237 votes after he polled 14,769.
2c640f4c604e1918: PETALING JAYA: Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM) akan menjalankan pemeriksaan ke atas sebuah kilang roti di Shah Alam susulan dakwaan keracunan makanan yang tular di media sosial.
KKM berkata, ia sedang menunggu keputusan analisis makmal berhubung produk terbabit dan akan memeriksa kilang itu bagi memastikan pematuhan terhadap Akta Makanan.
"Tindakan penguatkuasaan sewajarnya akan diambil, sekiranya terdapat bukti pelanggaran atau risiko keselamatan makanan," katanya dalam kenyataan.
KKM memaklumkan pihaknya telah mendapatkan penjelasan daripada Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd berhubung dakwaan keracunan makanan itu.

"Menurut syarikat (itu), siasatan dalamannya tidak menemui sebarang penyimpangan proses pengeluaran, perubahan resipi atau ketidakpatuhan terhadap prosedur operasi standard (SOP) dan kawalan keselamatan makanan bagi produk terlibat."
Katanya, beberapa produk telah diambil untuk tujuan analisis makmal.
Semalam, Gardenia dalam kenyataan berkata, pihaknya telah menemui pelanggan terbabit dan mengambil sampel roti berkenaan untuk dianalisis.
"Jabatan berkaitan sedang meneliti maklumat, rekod pengeluaran serta kawalan kualiti bagi mengenal pasti fakta sebenar dan menentukan tindakan susulan.

"Kami juga ingin memberi jaminan kepada pengguna bahawa tiada perubahan dibuat terhadap resipi atau formulasi produk kami dan prosedur keselamatan makanan serta kawalan kualiti yang ditetapkan terus dilaksanakan."
Gardenia berkata, ia komited memberi kerjasama kepada KKM dalam siasatannya.
Terdahulu, seorang pengguna Threads mendakwa anaknya jatuh sakit selepas makan roti dikeluarkan syarikat itu.
2caf9f107a581786: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 8 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is awaiting laboratory analysis results and will conduct follow-up inspections at the Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd factory to verify compliance with the Food Act 1983 following complaints of alleged food poisoning involving the company’s products.

In a statement today, MOH said preliminary investigations were underway into complaints circulating on social media and media reports of alleged food poisoning after consumption of Gardenia products, particularly Gardenia Original Classic White Bread and Twiggies Choc-A-Lot.

“MOH has sought an explanation from Gardenia Bakeries (KL). According to the company, its internal investigation found no deviations in production processes, recipe changes or non-compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) and food safety controls for the products concerned.

“Traceability of the products involved remains limited as the batch numbers and expiry dates provided were incomplete. However, the remaining products and their packaging were collected with the complainants’ consent for laboratory analysis,” MOH said.
MOH stressed that the company’s findings were based on its internal investigation and could not yet be used as the basis for a definitive conclusion on the cause of the symptoms reported.
The ministry also assured that appropriate enforcement action would be taken if evidence of legal violations or risks to food safety were found.

Meanwhile, MOH advised the public against making speculation that could cause confusion, while individuals experiencing symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhoea or discomfort after consuming the suspected products were urged to seek medical attention immediately and report the matter to the nearest District Health Office.
Food safety complaints can be channelled through the Public Complaints Management System (SiSPAA) at https://moh.spab.gov.my/ or the Food Safety and Quality Programme’s Facebook page.
Recently, a Threads user claimed to have suffered food poisoning after consuming two Gardenia products, sparking public attention and discussion on social media over their safety. — Bernama
51aa7d9c3c1745f6: ISTANBUL: Polish President Karol Nawrocki declared two days of national mourning following a shooting in Krakow that left six dead and many others injured, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
"The President signed a decree ... declaring a period of national mourning throughout the territory of the Republic of Poland on November 8 and 9," the president's spokesman said in a statement.
A gunman said to have been inspired by far-right ideology killed six people, including a British national, and injured many others in an attack in the busy centre of Poland's second-largest city.
Police said the attacker drove on to Main Market Square in Krakow on Saturday afternoon and fired randomly at people.
The mourning period began at midnight, with national flags lowered to half-mast.
Websites have added black ribbons to their logos and adopted more subdued colour schemes, while radio and television broadcasters have adjusted their programming schedules.
Entertainment events have also been cancelled as a mark of respect for the victims. — BERNAMA
2b04fc61c54ef043: KUALA LUMPUR: Affin Hwang Investment Bank Bhd (Affin Hwang IB) has trimmed its earnings forecast for Public Bank Bhd between one and 10 per cent for 2026 through 2028.
This is after considering the bank's Hong Kong goodwill impairment this year and muted expectations on non-interest income and net interest margin.
The firm noted that the bank's nine-month earnings of RM5.35 billion came in within expectations.
Public Bank's third quarter earnings dropped 3.8 per cent to RM1.77 billion on the back of modest income growth and normalised provisions.
Non-interest income was dragged by a weaker trading income in tandem with weaker treasury asset valuations.

Affin Hwang IB said the bank's asset quality was broadly stable at a 0.55 per cent gross impaired loans (GIL) ratio, although absolute GIL inched by 12 per cent year-on-year (YoY) stemming from Malaysia and Cambodia.
A three basis point (bp) rise in household sector GILs was led by mortgages and hire purchase likely a product of cost pressures.

The non-household sector clocked a mild 1.0bp YoY rise in GIL ratio on higher working capital and commercial property purchase loans GILs in the wholesale and retail trade as well as real estate sectors.

"Public Bank was more downbeat on targets owing to keen rates competition and potentially higher near-term credit costs, signalling wider net interest margin compression, more refined non-interest income growth and higher credit costs.
"Loan growth is likely to exceed its four to five per cent target," it said in a note.
Affin Hwang IB expects earnings recovery in 2027 and valuations to be supported by capital returns and dividends.
The firm kept its "Buy" call on the stock with a lower target price of RM5.45.

a4c26889875fee8a: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) must provide detailed evidence to support its claim that it had fulfilled 97 per cent of the promises in its manifesto for the 15th Melaka State Election in 2021, said Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari.

He called on Melaka BN to provide a comprehensive list of its achievements for the people to assess the actual implementation status of the 103 initiatives outlined in the manifesto across five main thrusts.

“The claimed achievements should be accompanied by a complete list showing the status and commitments so that voters can make their own assessment,” he said at PH’s daily press conference at the coalition’s main operations room in Bukit Baru here today.

Adly, who is defending the Bukit Katil seat in the 16th Melaka State Election, said transparency in presenting manifesto achievements was important to ensure that every commitment announced by the government could be assessed based on actual implementation outcomes, rather than merely percentage figures.
He also said that based on a summary of the Auditor-General’s Report, the Melaka government suffered a deficit in 2024, with revenue of RM490 million against expenditure of RM519 million.
He said the figures underscored the importance of prudent financial management, as well as ensuring that every spending decision was properly documented and produced verifiable results.

“Sometimes we may be able to increase revenue, but expenditure management must also be given priority… that is why, according to the 2024 records, the (state government’s) revenue was RM490 million, while expenditure stood at RM519 million,” he said.
According to Adly, Melaka recorded a financial surplus of RM50 million in 2019 when he led the state administration.
He said PH, through its “Melaka Rumah Kita” aspirations, was offering clean, transparent and integrity-driven governance, including ensuring that every ringgit of public funds was managed prudently.
He said voters were entitled to clear information on the state government’s achievements so that they could make informed assessments ahead of the state election.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/ — Bernama
a55a64fa98ee1577: JASIN: Wanita Umno menepis dakwaan calon Barisan Nasional (BN) DUN Rim, Khaidirah Abu Zahar menggunakan dana kerajaan untuk mempengaruhi undi yang disifatkannya isu sengaja dicipta pembangkang.
Ketua Penerangan Wanita Umno, Rosni Zahari, berkata bantuan yang disampaikan kepada penduduk di kawasan itu daripada Majlis Bandaraya Melaka Bersejarah (MBMB), bukannya seperti didakwa.
"Penduduk di situ kata bukan Dira datang bersalam-salam dengan kita dan nak beri apa-apa bantuan. Yang memberi bantuan itu sebenarnya pihak majlis bandaraya, bukannya Dira.
"Saya rasa itu bukan isunya. Itu isu yang cuba diwujudkan pihak pembangkang kerana mereka mahu mencari kesalahan," katanya kepada FMT dalam kempen BN di Merlimau.
Pada 3 Nov lalu, Pengerusi Pakatan Harapan Melaka, Adly Zahari dilaporkan menggesa Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya menyiasat dakwaan sogokan menerusi pengagihan bakul makanan sempena Deepavali di DUN Rim.

PH membuat laporan polis terhadap Khaidirah pada hari sama atas dakwaan berkempen menggunakan premis dan jentera kerajaan ketika menghadiri majlis penyampaian sumbangan kepada kira-kira 30 penerima sempena sambutan Deepavali.
Rosni mengingatkan pembangkang supaya berkempen secara baik dan tidak mencipta isu atau menyebarkan fitnah demi meraih kemenangan.
Ini kerana, jelasnya, pengundi Melaka semakin matang dan mampu menilai pihak yang benar-benar memperjuangkan kebajikan mereka sepanjang tiga tahun pentadbiran kerajaan negeri.

Mengulas perkembangan kempen calon BN, tegasnya, beliau tidak bimbang dengan kedudukan Khaidirah berdasarkan prestasinya yang sangat baik sebelum ini dan yakin mampu mendapat kemenangan lebih besar berbanding pilihan raya lalu.
Rosni turut yakin dengan dua lagi calon Wanita Umno, Siti Aisyah Mahmood yang bertanding di kerusi Pangkalan Batu dan Tuminah Kadi (Pantai Kundor).

Katanya, Siti Aisyah yang menggantikan Kalsom Nordin tidak asing kepada pengundi kerana sudah lama melakukan kerja lapangan, selain merupakan naib ketua Wanita Umno Hang Tuah Jaya dan pembantu kepada Kalsom ketika menyandang kerusi itu.
Menurutnya, Tuminah yang juga penyandang kerusi Pantai Kundor mempunyai rekod perkhidmatan baik dan mendapat sokongan nelayan setempat.
Jelasnya, dakwaan pembangkang kononnya Tuminah mengabaikan kebajikan nelayan tidak benar berdasarkan maklum balas diterimanya ketika turun menemui golongan itu bersama calon.

Beliau berkata, isu lesen bot nelayan yang dibangkitkan penduduk bukan dalam bidang kuasa Tuminah, sebaliknya di bawah kerajaan persekutuan dan beliau sudah menghubungi Lembaga Kemajuan Ikan Malaysia untuk membantu menyelesaikannya.
95035af7ae4f1f29: KUALA LUMPUR: Despite the relatively small Hindu population in Sabah and Sarawak, Deepavali celebrations today brought together people from diverse backgrounds, reflecting a strong spirit of unity.

The Department of Statistics Malaysia estimates that Sarawak has about 5,000 Indians, accounting for 0.2 per cent of its 2.53 million population, while Sabah has around 6,000, or 0.2 per cent of its 3.77 million residents, based on 2026 data.
This year's celebrations were a different experience for serviceman R. Ruhthiran, 20, as he celebrated the festival away from his family in Klang, Selangor, for the first time.
Stationed in SARAWAK, at Penrissen Camp in Kuching, the second of five siblings said being away from his family was part of the demands of military service.

"I miss my family, but I am enjoying my time here. Being separated from loved ones is part of life as a soldier," he told Bernama before attending prayers at the Sri Maha Mariamman Temple in Batu Lintang.
He said Deepavali celebrations typically began with an early-morning oil bath, followed by wearing new clothes and attending prayers at the temple around 8 am.
"My mother usually prepares idli and thosai for breakfast," he said, adding that the family would return home after prayers before visiting relatives to celebrate together.
Ruhthiran expressed gratitude to his seniors for helping him locate a temple, making it easier to fulfil his religious obligations.
For Kuching resident Pramod Kumar, 67, Deepavali remains a meaningful occasion, though celebrations are more modest because of the state's relatively small Hindu population.

"We usually start the day with prayers at the temple, followed by a family gathering to celebrate Deepavali and seek blessings," he said, adding that Kuching celebrates Deepavali much the same way as Peninsular Malaysia and India, but on a smaller scale.
In SABAH, people of various ethnicities and faiths gathered at the Sri Pasupathinath Alayam Temple in Kota Kinabalu to join in the Deepavali festivities.
First-time visitor Geoffrey Lo, 50, said he was excited to experience the Deepavali celebrations at the temple.
"This is my first time here and I am really excited... the food is delicious too," he said.
Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor is scheduled to attend the 2026 Deepavali gathering at the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) at noon today. — BERNAMA

35eb3b5eb03571c4: PUTRAJAYA: The Health Ministry is awaiting laboratory analysis results and will conduct follow-up inspections at the Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd factory to verify compliance with the Food Act 1983.
This is being done following complaints from consumers who reported feeling unwell after eating certain Gardenia products.

In a statement, MoH said preliminary investigations were underway following complaints circulating on social media and media reports of ill effects after the consumption of Gardenia products, particularly Gardenia Original Classic White Bread and Twiggies Choc-A-Lot.

"The ministry has sought an explanation from Gardenia Bakeries (KL). According to the company, its internal investigation found no irregularities in the production process, changes to the recipe or non-compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) and food safety controls for the products concerned.

"Product traceability efforts remain limited as the manufacturing batch details and expiry dates provided were incomplete. However, the remaining products and their packaging have been collected with the complainants' consent for laboratory analysis," said the ministry.
The ministry said the company's findings were based on its internal investigation and could not yet form the basis for a definitive conclusion on the cause of the reported symptoms.
The ministry also gave its assurance that appropriate enforcement action would be taken if there was evidence of any breach of the law or risks to food safety.
Meanwhile, it advised the public against speculation that could cause confusion.

It advised those experiencing symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhoea or discomfort after consuming the suspected products to seek medical attention immediately and report the matter to their nearest District Health Office.

Complaints related to food safety can also be submitted through the Public Complaints Management System (SiSPAA) at https://moh.spab.gov.my/ or via the Food Safety and Quality Programme's Facebook page.
Yesterday, Gardenia said it was investigating complaints from consumers following claims on social media that several children had fallen ill after consuming its products.

The company said its team had met with one of the consumers concerned to better understand the reported incident and obtain further information. It had also collected the relevant products for examination as part of its ongoing investigation.

44ece7d12b0abaf2: PETALING JAYA: Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) bertindak wajar mempersoalkan susunan kata dalam perintah pelepasan Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur melibatkan bekas perdana menteri, Najib Razak, kata beberapa peguam dan pakar undang-undang.
Peguam Razlan Hadri Zulkifli, berkata timbul kekeliruan ketara dan perbezaan tafsiran dalam kalangan orang ramai berhubung penggunaan perkataan 'pelepasan' (discharge) dalam perintah mahkamah itu.

Beliau berkata, Peguam Negara Dusuki Mokhtar tidak mencabar keputusan Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan, sebaliknya hanya memohon penjelasan mengenai tafsiran yang betul bagi perintah berkenaan.

"Kita mesti membenarkan peguam negara mendapatkan penjelasan diperlukan. Sekiranya segalanya berjalan mengikut saluran betul, Najib akan menjalani baki hukuman kes SRC beliau di kediamannya di Langgak Duta," katanya kepada FMT.
"Saya tidak fikir ini satu masalah yang tidak boleh diatasi. Pada pandangan saya, peguam negara bertindak mengikut tradisi terbaik jabatannya.
"Saya beranggapan tiada sebarang kesalahan untuk peguam negara membangkitkan isu ini. Malah, ia langkah terpuji. Kita sepatutnya bersyukur kerana mempunyai seorang peguam negara yang berhati-hati."
Beliau menyeru penyokong Najib agar bersabar, sambil menegaskan perkara sedemikian belum pernah berlaku.

Seorang lagi peguam, A Srimurugan, berkata perkataan 'pelepasan' dalam perintah mahkamah itu bersifat kabur, manakala ketiadaan peruntukan khusus di bawah Kanun Prosedur Jenayah memburukkan lagi keadaan.

“Mengapa kita tidak boleh tafsirkan begitu sahaja perkataan pelepasan itu? Ini kerana tiada peruntukan dalam kanun tersebut untuk menangani perkara ini. Apabila Yang di-Pertuan Agong memerintahkan seseorang menjalani hukuman bawah tahanan rumah, adakah itu bermakna orang tersebut dilepaskan?
“Sebab itulah peguam negara kini menunjukkan timbul masalah. Apa yang dilakukan peguam negara adalah tepat.
“Beliau berkata disebabkan kekaburan berkenaan, AGC perlu merujuk kembali kepada mahkamah, sama ada melalui semakan semula atau memohon penjelasan mengenai maksud perintah tersebut,” katanya.
Tegasnya, isu itu bukan berpunca daripada pihak istana mahupun peguam negara, sebaliknya daripada cara peguam Najib mendapatkan perintah berkenaan daripada pendaftar jenayah Mahkamah Tinggi.
“Situasi Najib ini merupakan sesuatu belum pernah berlaku. Peguam Najib sepatutnya memohon jenis perintah yang berbeza, tetapi beliau tidak berbuat demikian,” katanya.

Sementara itu, Ketua Kluster Tadbir Urus dan Undang-undang Majlis Profesor Negara, Nik Ahmad Kamal Nik Mahmood, berkata peguam negara tidak mahu perkataan 'pelepasan' diinterpretasikan sebagai membawa maksud Najib telah bebas sepenuhnya daripada sabitan kes SRC.

Beliau berkata, penjelasan adalah perlu bagi mengelakkan kekeliruan berterusan dalam kalangan awam, terutama mengenai hakikat Najib masih perlu menjalani baki hukumannya bawah tahanan rumah sehingga Ogos 2028.
“Timbul perdebatan dalam ruang awam yang menggambarkan seolah-olah Najib telah dibebaskan daripada sabitan kes SRC.
“Peguam negara tidak mahu perdebatan ini dieksploitasi untuk tujuan politik. Jadi, beliau mahu susunan kata tersebut diperjelas,” katanya.
Nik Ahmad Kamal turut berkata, peguam negara wajar membangkitkan isu berkenaan selaras peranannya sebagai penasihat undang-undang kerajaan.
Jumaat lalu, Umno umum menjelaskan denda RM50 juta dikenakan ke atas Najib sebagai sebahagian syarat membenarkannya menjalani baki hukuman penjara kes SRC bawah tahanan rumah.

AGC kemudiannya menyeru pelaksanaan tahanan rumah Najib ditangguhkan sehingga semakan semula ke atas 'persoalan undang-undang yang kompleks' berhubung perintah pelepasan dikeluarkan Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur.

AGC menyebut perintah pelepasan Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur kepada jabatan penjara yang menyatakan: “Dan bahawasanya denda tersebut yang berjumlah RM50 juta kini telah dibayar ke mahkamah ini: Ini adalah untuk memberi kuasa kepada anda untuk melepaskan Najib Razak […] serta-merta.”
Perintah mahkamah sama turut menyatakan Najib perlu menjalani baki hukuman bawah tahanan rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028.

“Justeru, timbul persoalan undang-undang mengenai skop dan kesan arahan pelepasan tersebut, khususnya sama ada pelepasan yang diperintahkan hanya berkaitan dengan pembayaran denda atau membolehkan baki hukuman penjara SRC International diteruskan melalui tahanan rumah, atau sama ada perintah tersebut membawa kesan hukuman dalam kes SRC International telah selesai," kata AGC.
AGC berkata, implikasi undang-undang daripada perintah tersebut sepatutnya dirujuk kepada mahkamah dengan kadar segera bagi mendapatkan keputusan dan arahan jelas.
d21d12add32c0c6c: PETALING JAYA: The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) was right to question the wording of the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s discharge order involving former prime minister Najib Razak, say several lawyers and a legal expert.
Lawyer Razlan Hadri Zulkifli said there had been considerable confusion and differing interpretations among the public over the use of the word “discharge” in the court order.
He said Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar was not challenging the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s decision but merely seeking clarification on the proper interpretation of the order.
“We must let the AG get the necessary clarification. If everything turns out as it should, Najib will serve the remainder of his SRC sentence at his Langgak Duta residence,” he told FMT.
“I don’t think it’s an insurmountable problem. I think the AG has acted in the best tradition of his office.
“I think there’s nothing wrong with the AG raising the issue. In fact, it is commendable. We should be thankful that we have a careful AG.”
He urged Najib’s supporters to be patient, saying the matter was unprecedented.

Another lawyer, A Srimurugan, said the word “discharge” in the court order was ambiguous, with the absence of a specific provision under the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) further complicating the matter.

“Why can’t we just decipher the word 'discharge'? It’s because there’s no provision in the CPC to address this. When the king orders someone to serve a sentence under house arrest, does that mean the person is discharged?
“This is why the AG is now pointing out that there is a problem. What the AG is doing is correct.
“He is saying that because of the ambiguity, the AGC has to go back to the court, either by way of revision or by requesting clarification on what the order means,” he said.
Srimurugan stressed that the issue did not originate from the palace or the AG, but from the manner in which Najib’s counsel obtained the order from the High Court’s criminal registry.
“Najib’s situation is unprecedented. Najib’s lawyer ought to have applied for a different kind of order, but he did not,” he said.

Meanwhile, National Council of Professors’ governance and law cluster head Nik Ahmad Kamal Nik Mahmood said the AG did not want the word “discharge” to be interpreted as meaning that Najib had been fully released from his SRC conviction.

He said clarification was necessary to prevent further public misunderstanding, particularly over the fact that Najib was still required to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 2028.
“There is a debate in the public sphere suggesting Najib has been freed from his SRC conviction.
“The AG did not want this debate to be exploited for political purposes. So he wants the wording clarified,” he said.
Nik Ahmad Kamal also said the AG was right to raise the issue in keeping with his role as the government’s legal adviser.
Last Friday, Umno paid the RM50 million fine imposed on Najib as part of the conditions allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC prison sentence under house arrest.
The AGC then called for Najib’s house arrest to be deferred until a review of “complex legal questions” over the discharge order issued by the High Court in Kuala Lumpur.

It highlighted the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Order of Discharge to the prisons department, which states: “And whereas the said fine amounting to RM50 million has now been paid into this court: This is to authorise you to discharge the said Najib Razak […] forthwith.”
The same court order also states that Najib is to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.

“The dispute arose on the scope and effect of the discharge order – whether it focused solely on the payment of the fine and allowed him (Najib) to serve the remaining SRC International sentence on house arrest, or if the discharge order meant that his (six-year) sentence had been completed,” the AGC said.
The AGC said the legal implications of the court order should be referred to the court immediately to obtain a clear determination and directions.

9d3abb54923f7f37: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) must provide detailed evidence to support its claim that it had fulfilled 97 per cent of the promises in its manifesto for the 15th Melaka State Election in 2021, said Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari.

He called on Melaka BN to provide a comprehensive list of its achievements for the people to assess the actual implementation status of the 103 initiatives outlined in the manifesto across five main thrusts.

"The claimed achievements should be accompanied by a complete list showing the status and commitments so that voters can make their own assessment," he said at PH's daily press conference at the coalition's main operations room in Bukit Baru here today.

Adly, who is defending the Bukit Katil seat in the 16th Melaka State Election, said transparency in presenting manifesto achievements was important to ensure that every commitment announced by the government could be assessed based on actual implementation outcomes, rather than merely percentage figures.
He also said that based on a summary of the Auditor-General's Report, the Melaka government suffered a deficit in 2024, with revenue of RM490 million against expenditure of RM519 million.
He said the figures underscored the importance of prudent financial management, as well as ensuring that every spending decision was properly documented and produced verifiable results.

"Sometimes we may be able to increase revenue, but expenditure management must also be given priority... that is why, according to the 2024 records, the (state government's) revenue was RM490 million, while expenditure stood at RM519 million," he said.
According to Adly, Melaka recorded a financial surplus of RM50 million in 2019 when he led the state administration.
He said PH, through its "Melaka Rumah Kita" aspirations, was offering clean, transparent and integrity-driven governance, including ensuring that every ringgit of public funds was managed prudently.
He said voters were entitled to clear information on the state government's achievements so that they could make informed assessments ahead of the state election.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10. — BERNAMA
28ffa2ec7bfeaa41: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 8 — The Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) has allocated RM600,000 to upgrade basic infrastructure and enhance youths' technical skills in Kampung Murni A under the 2026 Madani Adopted Village initiative.
Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the programme reflected the federal government's commitment to inclusive national development, including in rural areas.

"The Madani Government introduced the Madani Adopted Village initiative based on a clear principle: national development must not leave rural and remote communities behind, while basic amenities and living standards in villages must be improved in a direct, tangible and immediate manner," he said.
He spoke at the 2026 NRES Madani Adopted Village handover ceremony in Kampung Murni A today, which included an allocation of RM500,000 to rebuild a community hall and upgrade a futsal court.
Arthur said the multi-purpose hall would facilitate community gatherings and activities, while the futsal court would promote an active lifestyle and help develop young local sporting talent.

In addition to infrastructure improvements, he said RM100,000 had been set aside for the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) on-the-job training programme in collaboration with Keningau GIATMARA.
"The hands-on training enabled youths in Kampung Murni A to develop technical skills and install 25 solar streetlights at strategic locations around the village.

569f56960b97c26e: SINGAPORE, Nov 8 — Longtime pasar malam stall Teochew Meat Puff will be shuttering after 40 years in business, with its final night market appearance taking place in Sengkang this month.
In a Facebook post shared on Oct 30, Teochew Meat Puff Pte Ltd said that this might just be their last run as they are looking to retire.
It had resumed business after a one-month break and are currently operating in an open field located opposite Fernvale Primary School.
The store wrote: “For those who have yet to try our meat puff, please kindly grab one to try before we retire from pasar malam and we won’t be operating forever. So we hope to see you again soon.”
The stall also thanked customers for their continuous support the last 40 years.
Teochew Meat Puff is open from 12pm to 9.30pm daily and will be in operation till Nov 14, it said.
A family-run stall by He Ying, his wife and their son, the stall specialises in deep-fried snacks commonly known as oyster fritters.

He Qiangde (transliterated), the stall’s second-generation owner, told Shin Min Daily News on Nov 5 that the family had been contemplating the closure for the past year or two, attributing it to his parent’s age.
“My parents are getting old, my father is nearly 90 years old, and I want them to be able to rest properly. After all, they’ve been doing this for 40 years.”

He also noted that the rising costs of ingredients and rental fees also contributed to the decision, revealing that their current sales figures are more than 50 per cent lower than before the pandemic.
“Often, we barely break even. It’s not like before the pandemic, when we could actually make a profit,” he said.
With the increasing number of night markets, he shared that it’s “hard to maintain a unique appeal” and that most of the crowd already thins out by 8pm.
While he and his parents feel a deep sense of reluctance about the closure, he expressed his gratitude for the support that customers have shown over the years.
Qiangde plans to seek other employment moving forward and is also keen on selling the family recipe.

“If anyone is interested now, I am open to selling the recipe, with the condition that I must teach it personally to ensure the quality of the oyster fritters is maintained,” he told the daily. — AsiaOne
bc1e039ce3de9379: BUTTERWORTH: Unusually heavy rain and strong winds caused ceiling leaks and rainwater intrusion in several buildings at Seberang Jaya Hospital last night.
