2bf27a5a0fed8b72: KOTA BARU: The 22-year-old Arulmigu Sivasubramaniyar Alayam temple in Jalan Hamzah here continues to draw devotees seeking blessings and fulfilling religious vows as Hindus celebrated Deepavali today.
The temple, regarded as the oldest Hindu temple in the district, was bustling with activity from 7am, with about 100 families expected to visit throughout the day.
Temple president Datuk Subramaniam Nacihaippan said the temple had been a focal point for the local Hindu community since its establishment in 2004.
"The temple has been serving the community for more than 20 years, and Deepavali is one of the most meaningful occasions for devotees to come together to offer prayers," he said.

The temple, whose foundation stone was laid by former Kelantan Menteri Besar, the late Tan Sri Nik Abdul Aziz Nik Mat, held prayers throughout the day, with two priests overseeing the religious ceremonies.
Today's prayers were handled by temple priests Annamalai Tamilselvan, 64, and Annamalai Subbiah, 50.
The morning prayers continued until 1pm before the temple resumes its religious activities from 7pm to 10pm, with special prayers for devotees seeking the fulfilment of their wishes.
Temple deputy president Vijaya Kumar Perunal said Deepavali was also an occasion for families to reunite and uphold their religious traditions.
Among the devotees was Dr Navanithan Ramakrishnan, who travelled from Kuala Lumpur with his wife, Dr Shri Rajeswari, and their two-year-old son, AdvaayaaRaam Navanithan.
The family returned to Kota Baru to celebrate Deepavali with their family.
"We came back to celebrate Deepavali together with the family and also to seek blessings at the temple," he said.
For resident R. Hareetaran, visiting the temple with his family during Deepavali has become an annual tradition.
He brought his wife, Shaarada Bairavi Jeyabalan and their four-year-old son, Vidhur to offer prayers.
Hareetaran said the annual visit was an important way to introduce his young son to Hindu practices and ensure that the tradition continued across generations.

"For my family and other devotees, the temple remains more than a place of worship, serving as a gathering point for the Hindu community in Kelantan to celebrate Deepavali, strengthen family ties and seek blessings for the year ahead," he added.
3bf9e00e1cd09e04: PETALING JAYA: Tiga kumpulan masyarakat sivil menyeru semua pihak memberi ruang kepada mahkamah menyelesaikan kekaburan undang-undang berhubung tahanan dalam rumah bekas perdana menteri, Najib Razak, sebelum pelaksanaan itu dijalankan.

Projek Sama, Bersih, dan Pusat Memerangi Rasuah dan Kronisme (C4 Center), berkata Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) telah membangkitkan kekaburan mahupun kekhilafan yang serius, disengajakan atau tidak, dalam perintah Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur bertarikh 6 Nov.
Dalam kenyataan bersama, kumpulan itu berkata susunan kata dalam perintah tersebut boleh menyebabkan hukuman penjara enam tahun Najib bagi kes SRC International dianggap telah selesai.
Katanya, sekiranya Najib dilepaskan secara tidak sah dalam kes SRC, hukuman penjara 15 tahun beliau bagi kes 1MDB-Tanore akan bermula dengan serta-merta.

Mereka turut memuji Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) yang cukup berwaspada dalam mengenal pasti kekaburan perintah Mahkamah Tinggi dan berharap perintah itu tidak digesakan untuk dilaksana dengan tekanan politik atau kempen awam.

Kumpulan berkenaan berkata, sebarang percubaan menghalang kekaburan atau kekhilafan itu daripada dicabar di mahkamah bakal mencabuli kedaulatan undang-undang—dan seterusnya menghakis keyakinan awam dan antarabangsa terhadap tatakelola yang baik serta ekonomi Malaysia.

"Menghalang kekaburan atau kekhilafan ini daripada dicabar di mahkamah, secara prinsipnya, mencabuli kedaulatan undang-undang, sekali gus mengubah sifat asas Malaysia sebagai sebuah negara Raja Berperlembagaan yang berteraskan demokrasi berparlimen," katanya.

Kumpulan tersebut berkata, perbezaan tafsiran terhadap peruntukan Perlembagaan dan undang-undang antara institusi suatu perkara biasa, justeru badan kehakiman mentafsir undang-undang dan menyelesaikan pertikaian perundangan.
Katanya, penangguhan secara singkat ini akhirnya akan memberi kelebihan kepada Najiib dari sudut pandangan awam.
"Pantang untuk Najib tergesa-gesa dengan proses ini sehingga terus menjejaskan kedaulatan undang-undang dan keyakinan awam terhadap demokrasi berparlimen," katanya.

Mereka turut menuntut AGC mengumumkan pandangan bertulis peguam negara berhubung permohonan tahanan di rumah Najib, di mana orang ramai berhak mengetahui bagaimana tahanan rumah terhadap Najib dikawal selia dan atas asas undang-undang yang mana.

Sebelum ini, AGC menegaskan permohonann penangguhan pelaksanaan tahanan rumah Najib bukan bertujuan mempertikai, membatal atau menggantung perintah pengampunan bersyarat yang diperkenankan Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

Dalam kenyataan, AGC berkata isu dipersoalkan adalah kesan undang-undang bagi perintah pelepasan dikeluarkan oleh Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur susulan pembayaran denda RM50 juta oleh Najib, pada Jumaat.
5365fa2c6e9b95fe: SINGAPORE, Nov 8 — A total of 195 individuals, including eight men and 187 women, have been arrested by the police for their alleged involvement in vice-related activities.

The police said on Sunday that the suspects, aged between 18 and 63, were nabbed during coordinated raids at 61 locations across Singapore during anti-vice operations conducted between Sept 14 and Oct 30.
16 vice abettors were among those arrested.
The operation was carried out by officers from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) with support from seven police land divisions.
The raid targeted massage establishments, public entertainment outlets, beauty salons, hotels and residential units.
During the operations, the police seized mobile phones, computers, vice-related paraphernalia and cash amounting to more than S$150,000.
Several bank accounts, containing more than S$600,000, have also been frozen.
Following the operations, a 41-year-old man was on Oct 23 charged for his involvement in facilitating vice activities, while investigations against the remaining 194 suspects are ongoing.
Vice syndicates are not simply a vice problem, CID director Senior Assistant Commissioner of Police (SAC) Julius Lim said.
Their activities are often linked to other forms of criminality and pose broader threats to public safety and security, he pointed out.
“As these syndicates increasingly exploit technology and operate across borders, our enforcement efforts must keep pace, both at home and in coordination with foreign partners,” SAC Lim said.

Those found guilty of offering or facilitating the provision by a woman or girl to another person of sexual services in Singapore in return for payment or reward could be jailed for up to five years, fined up to S$100,000, or both.

The offence of procuring any woman for the purpose of prostitution; living wholly or in part on the earnings of the prostitution of another person; soliciting, receiving or agreeing to receive any gratification as an inducement or reward for providing any service, and who by providing that service does or will aid the prostitution of another person, carries a penalty of up to seven years’ imprisonment and a fine of up to S$100,000. — AsiaOne
025fde7b810e3a46: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 8 — A day after Istana Negara said Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon order was clear and unambiguous, Johor Umno Youth has turned its sights on the Attorney General (AG).
The Johor wing chief Noor Azleen Ambros said the AG must answer for how the Pardons Board’s September 18 decision was carried out, The Star reported today.
“Johor Umno Youth fully supports the firm stance taken by Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim on the matter,” Noor Azleen was quoted as saying.
“The Istana Negara statement issued on Saturday demonstrated that the King had carried out his duties and responsibilities in accordance with the Federal Constitution.”
He voiced disappointment with the way the matter was handled, saying it was careless and gave the impression of an attempt to sidestep the board’s ruling.
As evidence, he pointed to Istana Negara and the Prime Minister’s Office having to issue separate statements on November 7 to set out the actual position.
Noor Azleen then turned to the AG saying the lapse was one of negligence.

“Johor Umno Youth urges the Attorney General to take responsibility for the lack of care and negligence in implementing this decision by honourably stepping down immediately,” he was quoted as saying.
He added that a police report had been lodged against the AG but The Star report gave no details.
Malay Mail was unable to independently verify the police report.
Stepping aside, he said, would let investigations proceed transparently and with integrity.

Najib was granted a conditional royal pardon on September 18 to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine, after the Pardons Board cut his original 12-year jail term and RM210 million fine to six years and RM50 million in 2024.

Umno said it had settled the fine, but Najib remained in Kajang Prison on November 6 after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) asked for his transfer to be deferred pending clarification of legal questions, including how the pardon affects his separate 1MDB sentence.

Istana Negara said yesterday that the pardon order was clear and that all its conditions had been fulfilled, while the AGC denied defying the King and said it was seeking clarity on legal uncertainties.
88444d6c6d25e107: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Bigger stage, louder singalongs and a birthday surprise made South Korean idol rock band QWER’s return to Malaysia a memorable afternoon for fans.

Less than a year after debuting in Kuala Lumpur at Zepp KL in January, the quartet returned yesterday, this time taking over Mega Star Arena as part of their second world tour, Rockation: Rocket Launch!!.

Comprising drummer Chodan, guitarist and keyboardist Hina, vocalist Siyeon and bassist Lee Ah-hee, QWER wasted little time getting the audience on their feet, opening the approximately 4pm show with Pioneer, Showdown and Bad Habit.
The members then greeted the estimated 3,000 fans, with Chodan setting the tone for the afternoon.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Fans queue outside the Mega Star Arena before QWER’s concert November 7. — Picture by Ian Jeremiah Patrick
“What’s up, Malaysia? Lama tak jumpa (long time no see),” she said, drawing cheers from fans who had been waiting to see the group perform in the country again.
From there, the concert moved through an energetic mix of tracks, including Free Dumb, G9JB, Discord, Bani Bani, Soda and Secret Diary.
The four members kept the momentum going with My Name Is Malguem, Dear, Goodbye My Sadness, T.B.H, D-Day, Harmony of Stars, Ceremony, Our Voyage, Dreamer and Yours Sincerely.
But the afternoon was not just about the music.
During some of the more upbeat numbers, giant inflatable balls were tossed into the audience, turning the crowd into part of the entertainment as fans bounced them around.
Concertgoers also kept the energy going by singing along to QWER’s songs while the group was briefly offstage for an outfit change.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

QWER merchandise given to concertgoers (left). Drummer Chodan, guitarist and keyboardist Hina, vocalist Siyeon and bassist Lee Ah-hee take the stage at Mega Star Arena for their second Malaysian concert (right). — Picture by Ian Jeremiah Patrick
As the concert approached its closing stretch, the four members returned for a final exchange with their Malaysian audience.
Hina said she was happy to meet the fans again, while Siyeon admitted that she was sad to be leaving.
“But don’t forget us,” she told the crowd.
Chodan, meanwhile, expressed her hope that QWER would be able to return more frequently.
“I wanna come back and have fun with you guys more often. Thank you so much for giving us another happy day.
“Sayang korang (I love you guys),” she added.
Lee Ah-hee also shared her appreciation, telling the audience, “Kami happy sangat (we are very happy),” before adding how much she loved the fans in Malaysia.
The show’s most personal moment, however, came when the concert took an unexpected turn for Chodan.
Just as the group was preparing for their customary final group photograph with the fans, a birthday cake appeared on stage, catching the drummer by surprise.
The audience joined in to sing the Korean birthday song, Saeng-il chuk-ha-ham-ni-da, turning the moment into an impromptu celebration shared between the group and their fans.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
QWER’s second Malaysian concert featured a surprise birthday celebration for drummer Chodan, prompting fans to join in a birthday singalong on November 7. — Picture by Ian Jeremiah Patrick
Chodan briefly thanked the fans, becoming emotional as she addressed the crowd.
She also jokingly pointed out that her birthday had already passed on November 1, but said celebrating it with Malaysian fans was a moment she would never forget.
It was a fitting highlight before QWER returned for their final three numbers, Overdrive, Fake Idol and Picaresque, bringing the concert to a close.

Since debuting in 2023, QWER has established themselves as one of South Korea’s rising girl groups, carving out a distinct musical identity through a combination of K-pop, pop rock and Japanese rock influences.

Their sound, which draws heavily from anime opening themes and Japanese pop culture, has helped them build an international following, with fans across markets including Japan, Thailand, Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia.
The group has also received recognition at several major music award ceremonies, including the K-World Dream Awards, MAMA Awards, Melon Music Awards and Asia Artist Awards.

With the Rockation: Rocket Launch!! tour continuing into 2027, QWER’s Malaysian return offered another opportunity to bring their music to fans outside South Korea — and, judging by the enthusiastic reception, their next visit is already something local fans can look forward to.
8e7115ae1e8f0dee: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Ayer Molek seat, Muhammad Hakimin Mokhtar, wants to develop the constituency into an education and employment hub to create more job opportunities for residents if elected in the 16th Melaka state election.

The 35-year-old Melaka Angkatan Muda Keadilan chief said Ayer Molek had considerable potential to attract higher education institutions, such as MARA colleges or polytechnics, as well as business establishments that could stimulate the local economy.

He said the proposal was among the ideas that emerged from his engagements with residents during the campaign, with difficulties finding employment within their own area frequently raised as a major concern.

“I want to offer ideas and initiatives to develop Ayer Molek into a hub for educational institutions and a business complex that could attract supermarket operators and outside companies to set up operations here, thereby boosting the local economy,” he told Bernama.

Muhammad Hakimin, who holds a Bachelor of Administrative Science (Hons) from Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) and is a former Jasin Municipal Council member, said the two initiatives could bring significant long-term benefits to the Ayer Molek community.

He also wants to ensure that the State Legislative Assembly Development and Coordination Committee (Japerun) complex functions as an open community service centre accessible to everyone, regardless of background or political affiliation.

“I want the Japerun in Ayer Molek to be more proactive as a one-stop centre where residents can raise problems, seek assistance or share their views without discrimination based on their background or political beliefs.
“To me, an elected representative should not only be present at certain times or during elections, but should always remain accessible when the community needs help,” he said.

Muhammad Hakimin also pledged to address 60 issues faced by residents, including internet connectivity, flooding and basic infrastructure problems which he said had yet to be resolved by previous leaderships.

He said he would seek effective and timely solutions by working closely with relevant agencies and the private sector, including through corporate social responsibility (CSR) programmes to secure additional support.

“I believe real development is not merely about bringing in major projects, but about how far they can resolve people’s everyday problems and improve the overall quality of life in the community,” he said.
Muhammad Hakimin is facing a straight fight against Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali for the Ayer Molek seat.
Polling is on Nov 14, with early voting set for Tuesday.
For updates on the state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
0871bdb7359562ee: KOTA BARU: The General Operations Force (GOF) arrested a man for possessing two hill mynas estimated to be worth RM50,000 without the required permits during Ops Taring Wawasan Kelantan at Kampung Banggol Pak Esah, Selising, Pasir Puteh, yesterday.
Hill mynas are classified as a 'Protected Wildlife' species and are highly sought after for their mimicry skills.

Southeast Brigade GOF commander, Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain, said intelligence personnel from GOF's Battalion 7 in Kuantan, Pahang, arrested the 32-year-old man following an operation at 5.45pm, which uncovered the birds in a shed beside the suspect's house.

"The man failed to produce any documents pertaining to ownership of the birds, which are believed to have been in his possession since 2019 after he bought them from a friend in Gua Musang," he said in a statement.
Ahmad Radzi said police also seized two bird cages estimated to be worth RM800.
He said the seized items and the suspect were handed over to the Kelantan Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) for further investigation and action.
The case is being investigated under Section 60(1)(a) of the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716).
He said the operation involved cooperation between the GOF and Kelantan Perhilitan to curb the possession of wildlife without permits.

8a5f3eca886230b1: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit parts of Terengganu, Pahang, Johor and Sabah until noon today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).

e6c78d4d5cf42e25: TOKYO: A strong 5.7-magnitude earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, injuring dozens of people, shattering windows and disrupting train services, officials and local media said.
The quake struck at 1.04 am in Shizuoka Prefecture, west of Tokyo, the Japan Meteorological Agency said. No tsunami warning was issued.
Authorities reported no deaths, but the quake shattered storefront windows and knocked items off shelves and caused transport disruption in parts of the country.
An emergency official in Aichi told AFP authorities had received 16 reports of mostly minor injuries.
Authorities in neighbouring Shizuoka said at least three women sought emergency medical care, including a woman in her nineties who injured her shoulder after falling from her bed during the shaking.
The local Chunichi Shimbun newspaper and Tokai Television separately reported at least 24 were hurt across the two regions.
In Toyohashi city in the Aichi region, windows of a car dealership were found shattered after the quake.
A large book store in Toyota city, also in Aichi, reported that its merchandise dropping from shelves.
The quake also forced temporary delays and suspensions of regional train services Sunday morning, including the Shinkansen bullet trains.
The quake was felt as far west as Osaka, where a foreign resident was taken to hospital after falling from a second-floor apartment when the shaking startled them, local media reported.
Officials in Osaka couldn't be reached for immediate comment.
Separately, a 4.3-magnitude quake struck the Kumamoto region at 10.53 am Sunday, the Meteorogolical Agency said.
There were no immediate reports of serious damage or injuries from the second quake.
The southwestern region is still trying to recover from a 7.1-magnitude tremor that killed 38 people, flattened homes and left tens of thousands without power in July.
Japan sits on the Pacific "Ring of Fire" and experiences hundreds of earthquakes every year.
The country is haunted by the massive 9.0-magnitude undersea quake in 2011, which triggered a tsunami that killed or left missing around 18,500 people and wrecked the Fukushima nuclear plant.
e2cafada2519c1c0: PETALING JAYA: Three civil society groups have urged all parties to allow the court to resolve legal ambiguities surrounding former prime minister Najib Razak’s house arrest before the arrangement is implemented.

Projek Sama, Bersih and the Center to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4 Center) said the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) had flagged a serious ambiguity, if not an error, in the Kuala Lumpur High Court order dated Nov 6.
In a joint statement, they said the wording of the order could result in Najib’s six-year prison sentence in his SRC International case being treated as having been completed.
They added that if Najib’s SRC sentence was legally deemed to have been completed, his 15-year prison term in the 1MDB-Tanore case should begin immediately.
They commended the AGC for identifying the ambiguity in the High Court order and said it should not face political pressure or punishment for carrying out its duties.
The groups warned that denying the AGC an opportunity to seek clarification would undermine the rule of law and erode public and international confidence in Malaysia’s governance and economy.

“Any attempt to make this ambiguity or error unchallengeable in court fundamentally undermines the rule of law and alters the basic character of Malaysia as a constitutional monarchy grounded in parliamentary democracy,” they said.
The groups said differing interpretations of constitutional and legal provisions between institutions were not unusual, and that it was the judiciary’s role to interpret and resolve such disputes.
They also said a brief delay to allow judicial clarification would ultimately benefit Najib if his house arrest arrangement was constitutionally and legally sound.
“Najib must refrain from rushing this process so as not to further undermine the rule of law and public confidence in parliamentary democracy,” they said.
The groups added that neither political pressure nor public campaigns should be allowed to hasten the implementation of an order whose legal status remained unsettled.

They also called on the AGC to disclose the attorney-general’s written opinion on Najib’s house arrest application, saying the public had a right to know the legal basis and regulatory framework governing the arrangement.

The groups reiterated their call for the full disclosure of all relevant documents, including the attorney-general’s written submission, the federal territories minister’s position, the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting and any legal or regulatory instruments regarding Najib’s house arrest.

“Those who truly believe in the validity of Najib’s pardon and house arrest should support this call,” they said, citing the Malay proverb: “Berani kerana benar, takut kerana salah (those who are right have nothing to fear).”

The AGC has stressed that its request to defer the implementation of Najib’s house arrest was not intended to dispute, set aside or suspend the conditional pardon order granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

In a statement yesterday, the AGC said the issue in question was the legal effect of the Order of Discharge issued by the Kuala Lumpur High Court following the payment of Najib’s RM50 million fine on Friday.

2356a1505af48223: RAMALLAH: The Palestinian Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Ministry has called for immediate international action to avert a deepening humanitarian and environmental catastrophe in the Gaza Strip as winter sets in.
The ministry warned that the crisis could claim more lives, particularly among children, older people and patients.

It said the continued Israeli aggression against Gaza had worsened the humanitarian crisis and prevented recovery efforts, noting that the first rainfall in recent hours exposed the dire conditions facing forcibly displaced Palestinians across the territory.

Nearly two million Palestinians are estimated to be living in about 270,000 tents and displacement sites across Gaza's governorates, with 60 to 85 per cent of the shelters worn out and unfit for use after nearly three years of displacement.
More than 400,000 displaced Palestinians live in high-risk areas vulnerable to flooding or located near the coastline, the ministry said.

It warned that the destruction of infrastructure, particularly sewage networks and drainage systems, further intensified the risks. Displaced residents also lack winter clothing, blankets, mattresses and safe heating, while electricity outages and fuel shortages leave them exposed to life-threatening cold and rainfall.

The ministry said international efforts must move beyond issuing appeals to immediately implementing relevant UN Security Council resolutions, including resolutions 2720 and 2803, and taking concrete measures to address Israeli violations.

It called for immediate pressure on Israel to open all border crossings and ensure the unrestricted entry of humanitarian assistance in quantities matching the needs of Gaza's population, with access guaranteed to all areas.
The ministry called for the urgent entry of fuel and equipment to operate water and sewage pumps, clear accumulated rainwater and wastewater, and carry out emergency flood interventions.

It urged the international community to provide winter shelter necessities, including temporary housing, weather-resistant tents, plastic sheeting, thermal insulation, and equipment to repair damaged homes.
It also called for the delivery of winter clothing, blankets, mattresses and heating supplies, particularly for infants, children, older people and patients.

The ministry urged an emergency health response, including medicines, medical supplies, clean water and sterilisation materials, alongside measures to combat water contamination and disease outbreaks linked to deteriorating environmental conditions. -BERNAMA
7c09db2f9ef61362: KUALA LUMPUR: What began as a small side business selling traditional Indian food has now become the main source of livelihood for Thirunavukkarasan Krishnana, 52, who took over the family business after his father suffered a stroke sometime in the 1990s.
The firstborn of three siblings said the incident happened while he was studying engineering at a private college in Petaling Jaya.
His father, then working at the Royal Selangor Golf Club, had started a part-time business selling food from a motorcycle before switching to a van a few years later to support the family.

Drawing on his experience helping his father with the business since his school days, Thirunavukkarasan was determined to continue the family business to support his family without disrupting his studies.
"After classes, I had to drive the pickup truck used for selling sugarcane juice and coconut drinks. I would drive the truck to college and head to the night market after classes.

"Among the places I used to trade were Taman Ikan Emas in Cheras, Taman Muda in Ampang, Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI) and the Kelana Jaya area," he told Bernama when met at his stall at the Putrajaya Permanent Farmers' Market recently.
Today, Thirunavukkarasan, assisted by his wife and children, sells a variety of traditional Indian food four times a week at several locations, including Putrajaya, Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman and TTDI.
Ever popular with customers, especially among the Malay community, some of his offerings include "vadey", "chapati", "thosai", "apam lenggang" and "murukku".
The father of three said his business flourished because his prices are affordable without compromising on quality. They are also halal-certified.
UMBI Project Boost
On his participation in the UMBI Project, the Kuala Lumpur-born entrepreneur said his business received more attention after he joined the initiative last year.

The UMBI Project is a three-year initiative implemented by the Institute of Malaysian and International Studies (IKMAS), Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), with the support of The Coca-Cola Foundation. It aims to help micro-entrepreneurs strengthen their business management foundations to build stable and consistent incomes.
Thirunavukkarasan said he learned how to obtain halal certification, prepare halal food and what halal means via the UMBI Project.

"Through the project, my business gained greater exposure as the initiative brought customers from all over Malaysia, including those who were previously unfamiliar with my products, to make purchases. Sales rose," he said.
Thirunavukkarasan hopes to pass on the family business to his children. But he said he has to ensure that they have the necessary know-how, coupled with education.
"I always remind them that if they find it difficult to secure a job after graduating from university, they are always welcome to continue the family business legacy," he said.
In conjunction with the Deepavali celebrations, Thirunavukkarasan's story reflects his love, sacrifice and his spirit of perseverance.

These are the foundations to preserve his heritage and family legacy. Together with his traditional halal food offerings, he continues to build a legacy enjoyed and cherished by a multi-racial community.

839700669c263672: KUALA LUMPUR: The British High Commission in Kuala Lumpur held its annual Remembrance Sunday service at Tugu Negara today to commemorate 81 years since the end of the Second World War and honour personnel and civilians who served in both world wars and other conflicts.
British High Commissioner to Malaysia Ajay Sharma said the sacrifices of service personnel and civilians reminded everyone not to take peace for granted.
"Today, we stand in quiet reflection to remember the courage and sacrifice of all those who served in times of war and conflict, especially those who never returned home.
"As we honour their memory, we renew our shared responsibility to work together towards a future defined by peace and understanding," he said.
The event brought together diplomatic and defence communities, including ambassadors, high commissioners, defence attachés and advisers.
Representatives from the Malaysian Armed Forces, Malaysian Veterans' Associations, local societies and schools were present.

The service included a performance by The International School @ ParkCity, reflections by Reverend Dinesh Natorajan, and readings of Rupert Brooke's "The Soldier" by Lieutenant General (R) Datuk Johnny Lim Eng Seng and Moina Michael's "We Shall Keep the Faith" by Kenneth Speldewinde.
United Kingdom Defence Adviser at the British High Commission Colonel James Green read Robert Laurence Binyon's "For the Fallen".
After observing two minutes of silence, the ceremony ended with the laying of wreaths at the base of the Cenotaph.
Remembrance Day is held on the second Sunday of November.
The milestone reminds the world of the enduring legacy of peace and the sacrifices made by generations past.

The service recognised the contributions of British, Commonwealth and other international military personnel in the two world wars and subsequent conflicts, as well as the vital role civilians played. - BERNAMA
ef02730f42c46995: KUCHING: Four incumbent Sarawak assemblymen will be defending their respective seats in the 13th Sarawak state election.

The announcement was made by Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg during a flag-off ceremony for a motorcycle convoy organised by the youth wing of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) at Kampung Matang Batu 10 here today.

"So, there is no need for me to joke around too much today. But looking at the faces of these four, I can see that they will remain Yang Berhormat," he said.

Also present at the event, which saw Abang Johari flag off a convoy of 100 motorcycles, were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni and Batang Lupar member of parliament Mohamad Shafizan Kepli.

Fazzrudin, who first became the Tupong assemblyman in 2016, will defend the seat for a third term after winning it in the 11th and 12th Sarawak elections.
In the 12th state polls, he secured 12,544 votes with a majority of 11,209, defeating PKR's Ahmad Nazib Johari, who polled 1,335 votes, and PBK's Chan Haong Yen, who received 836 votes.
Ibrahim, meanwhile, was first elected as the Satok assemblyman in the 12th state election, replacing Abang Johari, who previously held the seat before moving to contest in Gedong.

Hamzah, who entered the State Legislative Assembly for the first time after winning Stakan in the 12th state election, secured 7,854 votes with a majority of 5,807.
He defeated PSB's George Young Si Ricord Junior, who received 2,047 votes, DAP's Leslie Ting Xiang Zhi with 524 votes, and PBK's Atet anak Dego, who polled 415 votes.

Martin was first elected as the Kedup assemblyman in the 10th state election in 2011. He has defended the seat in three consecutive elections, including the 12th state election, when he secured 5,178 votes with a majority of 3,566.
In the 12th state election, Martin defeated PSB's Dominic Dado Sagin, who received 1,612 votes, PBK's Stephen Sungan with 745 votes, and DAP's Learry Jabul, who polled 640 votes.

In Klang, one PPS remained open at Dewan Masjid Al-Taqwa, Bukit Kapar, housing 32 victims from eight families.

71d82eb23b3356a6: MONTEVIDEO, Nov 8 — Pope Leo XIV on Saturday slammed the deaths of children in areas of wealthy Uruguay gripped by drug violence and urged young people to “dare” to get married, on the second day of his South American tour.
Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the 71-year-old pontiff is on a 12-day tour of the continent where he served nearly two decades as a missionary.
On Saturday, he visited the crime-blighted Montevideo neighborhood of Casavalle.
The murder rate in the impoverished district is four times the national average and residents spoke movingly of the dangers they faced, like commonplace gun violence.
Katherine Silva’s voice cracked with emotion as she told the pope about the violence and abuse she had suffered as a child.
After ending up homeless at 15, the young mother said she “went through very dark times” and “nearly died.”
“There are children in Uruguay who do not go to school for fear of never returning home,” Leo said.
“In a country as rich in resources as this, children should never have to go to bed hungry... Much less should they have to suffer violence to the point of losing their lives,” he added.
The murder rate in Uruguay, one of Latin America’s safest and wealthiest countries, has risen sharply in recent years due to its growing role in the cocaine trade.
Riddled with bullets
Claudia, a 33-year-old nurse who did not wish to give her surname, described to AFP once seeing a motorcycle pull up in front of her house “and riddle someone with bullets.”
“You don’t know what to do when your children see a body lying there. It’s become very normalised,” she said.
As police helicopters flew overhead, locals waved and cheered to welcome the head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who blessed 12 new low-income houses financed by the Church.
“Being here with you makes me feel at home, and brings back memories of the visits I made to various communities as a missionary,” Leo told residents, who
At a candle-lit prayer vigil on Saturday evening in Montevideo’s Centenario stadium, he remarked on the “advance of secularisation” in the world’s most Catholic continent.
Sharply falling fertility rates in Latin America — down from nearly six children per woman in the 1950s to 1.8 children in 2024 — could spell further decline in the Catholic population.
“Young people, dare to take the step of marrying and starting a family yourselves. Don’t be afraid of ‘forever’”! Leo told the packed 60,000-capacity football venue.
“Having the pope among us is an amazing goal!” Montevideo Archbishop Daniel Sturla told the crowd.
“Pope Leo, we love you so much!” the worshippers chanted.
Mad about mate

Latin America is the world’s most Catholic continent but the number of people who define themselves as such has plummeted in the past 30 years, from 80 per cent to 55 per cent, a Latinobarometro poll showed.
Celebrating mass in the northwesterncity of Paysandu, Leo called on Catholics in largely secular Uruguay to be “bridge builders.”
He drew applause by paying homage to the local tradition of sharing a herbal infusion called mate, sipped from a gourd with a metal straw.
“Mate has even made its way to Rome!” he joked.
At the Catholic University of Uruguay, he returned to a key theme of his papacy: the importance of ensuring AI is put at the service of human dignity.
The pope warned of “dehumanisation” through the use of AI in education, and urged schools and university to place the “person before the algorithm.”
US-born Leo’s tour had been in doubt after he was diagnosed with a cancerous tumour, but on the flight from Rome to Montevideo he cheerfully told journalists he was “in fairly good shape.”
His tour will take him to Argentina, home of the late Pope Francis, on Sunday and then to Peru, where he served as bishop and which claims the pope as one of its own. — AFP
a9f37bd35123c877: KUALA LUMPUR: A broken toy car brought a young child to tears, but a kind gesture from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim soon turned the situation around.
In a video that has since gone viral on Threads, user @heylyzarashid shared the moment Anwar approached her upset nephew, who was crying after his toy car broke.
Rather than simply offering words of comfort, Anwar handed the youngster RM50 and told him to use it to buy a new toy car.
"Your toy car is broken. Atok will get you another one. Keep this one (the broken toy) and use this (the money) to buy a new one, something nicer and bigger, okay?" he said.
Anwar's wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, was also present during the interaction.
Also in attendance were Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri and her deputy, Lim Hui Ying.
The incident took place during the National Family Month 2026 celebration at the Selangor International Trade Centre yesterday.

In her post, Heylyzarashid wrote: "Keeping this here as a memory. PMX (Anwar) was comforting my nephew, who was crying uncontrollably after his toy car broke. PMX then gave him RM50 and told him to buy a new car."
The gesture appeared to lift the child's spirits, turning an upsetting moment into a memorable encounter.
The video also drew reactions from social media users, with many praising the Prime Minister's spontaneous gesture.
One Threads user commented: "No status or rank, just a grandfather who could not bear to see a young child crying."

Another user wrote: "You must be so proud to have met PMX in person. This will be one of the most meaningful memories for this little one. When you grow up, watch this video again and remember how PMX gave you cash on the spot and told you to buy a new toy car."
4bb67c6239bd744f: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Two women were injured when a fire tore through a two-storey restaurant along Jalan Tun Sambanthan in Brickfields early this morning.

c892d50d2de7949c: AUCKLAND: New Zealand faced the prospect Sunday of weeks or even months of political wrangling after a knife-edge election that produced no clear winner.
Prime Minister Christopher Luxon declared his right-wing coalition has a mandate to form the country's next government -- while conceding results remained too close to call definitively.

Preliminary results have his National party winning the most seats, giving them a very slim majority of just two if combined with their coalition partners, the populist NZ First and the libertarian ACT.
"New Zealanders have given us the biggest seats in parliament, forty-two seats as it stands today, and a pathway to form a government," Luxon told journalists on Sunday.
"There's no doubt about it. We've got a mandate."
He said his National party had done well given the war in the Middle East and subsequent global fuel shock that has been widely blamed for New Zealand's economic difficulties.
"What we achieved, I think, was pretty good last night."
Opposition Labour Party leader Chris Hipkins has joked that while the country had spoken, "it may take us a little bit longer to figure out exactly what it is that you've said".
But the results show he has only a very narrow path to power for his left-wing grouping, which also includes the Green Party and the Maori party.
'Everyone's over politics'
Luxon will run a caretaker government until the final votes are announced on Nov 27.
"I think everyone's over politics, so let's all just have a bit of a break for the next three weeks," he said.

That final tally will include nearly 400,000 so-called "special votes" -- among them around 100,000 votes cast overseas and by people within New Zealand but outside the local electorate in which they live.
Historically, special votes leaned left, potentially giving the Labour or Green parties an additional one or two seats at the expense of the right-bloc.
This week's knife-edge poll drew intense attention to the country's minor parties, in particular the upstart centrist Opportunity Party.
Under the country's mixed-member proportional representation (MMP) system, voters must tick two options -- a general party list as well as an individual member to represent their electorate.
Results put Opportunity winning seven seats, potentially giving the party a kingmaker role in the next government.
Luxon said Sunday that while it was "unlikely" he would need the party to form a government, he was willing to work with leader Qiulae Wong on issues on which they agree.
"We can work with our current coalition partners to form the government," he said.
"What I've also said, though, is that there is a need for us to go forward in cross-party collaboration in a lot deeper way."
Many Kiwis are struggling to make ends meet -- the price of basic goods remains stubbornly elevated, and unemployment at its highest in more than a decade.
c4062d1bb81f902e: MIAMI: Inter Miami's Lionel Messi won his second consecutive MLS Golden Boot award on Saturday after the defending champions took second place in the Eastern Conference with a wasteful 3-3 draw against Charlotte on the final day of the regular season.
The Argentine superstar did not score but set up the first two goals at Miami's Nu Stadium, both from corners, to help procure his club a home-field advantage for the first two playoff rounds.

Messi's 26 goals this season were enough to make him the first back-to-back MLS Golden Boot award winner. Petar Musa of Dallas was second on 22, not scoring in his club's 3-1 home victory over Colorado.
Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul racked up three first-half strikes for Inter Miami before Liel Abada's brace soon after the break sparked a comeback sealed by Rodolfo Aloko's late strike.

Runaway overall leaders Nashville broke the all-time MLS points record for a season with a whopping 77 after beating Cincinnati 2-0. At 23-3 with eight drawn, Nashville won the East and broke the mark of 74 points set by Miami in 2024.
Miami finished second in the East on 60 points as third-place New England failed to take advantage of Inter's draw with a surprise 1-0 loss at Orlando to end on 58.

Messi's men will face Columbus to begin the MLS playoffs. Other East matchups send New England against Philadelphia, Charlotte against Chicago and top seed Nashville against the wild-card winner, Orlando or Cincinnati.
Columbus took advantage of the Cincinnati loss with a 4-3 victory at Chicago to finish seventh and avoid the wild card round.
At Miami, Messi's 14th-minute corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte's Luca de la Torre, who spooned it up for Fray to open the scoring.
Another Messi corner in the 33rd minute found Suarez wide open at the near post. The Uruguayan glanced in his header for 2-0.
De Paul made it three before halftime, but Abada pulled back a goal for the visitors early and bagged a second in the 55th minute.
In the 90th, Aloko bagged the equalizer, responding first to the ball as Smalls's shot ricocheted off the post.
A visibly frustrated Messi hit the post in stoppage time before Aloko came inches from bagging an unlikely winner with a thunderous shot into the outside netting.
- Seattle, Real advance -

Western Conference champion Vancouver beat Canadian rivals Montreal 2-0 to finish second overall, giving the Whitecaps a home-field edge if they should face Inter Miami in a rematch of last year's MLS Cup final.
There were six teams fighting for the last three Western Conference playoff spots on "Decision Day" with every MLS squad on the pitch.

Portland, Colorado and the Los Angeles Galaxy needed only to win to secure a playoff berth but only Portland did so, the Timbers winning 2-0 at Austin while Real Salt Lake beat the Galaxy 2-1 and Colorado fell at Dallas, which allowed Real into the post-season.

Seattle claimed the other spot with a 2-1 home win over Los Angeles FC. Albert Rusnak scored in the first minute and assisted on Sebastian Gomez's goal in the 31st for seattle and Eddie Segura's response in the 82nd minute was too little too late.
Minnesota beat visiting San Jose 3-1 but joined the Galaxy a point shy of the last-in Real Salt Lake.
Opening Western Conference playoff pairings find Vancouver against the Seattle-Salt Lake wildcard winner, Dallas against Portland, LAFC against St. Louis and Houston against San Jose. - AFP

55b7b7864edbdb02: KRAKÓW, Nov 8 — Six people were killed and at least 15 wounded on Saturday when a gunman opened fire in the landmark historic centre of Poland’s second city of Krakow, in the country’s deadliest shooting in decades.

Three bodies — of two women and a man — were later found at the suspect’s home, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said, adding there was “much to suggest that they are members of the (suspect’s) immediate family”.
Tusk also announced Poland would hold two days of mourning over the shooting that he called an act of “terrorism”.
Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said the gunman appeared to be “fascinated by far-right ideologies”.
A British national was among the killed, according to Polish police chief, Marek Boron, and five foreigners were among the wounded in hospital, the authorities said.
“Two people who have not yet been identified,” Boron said referring to the victims killed.
Britain’s Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was “shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting”.
“My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence,” he wrote on X.
The suspect — a Polish citizen born in 2002 — drove a car onto Krakow’s Main Market Square and began shooting at random people, said police.
Two officers were wounded as they tried to stop the man, the police said, before shooting the suspect who was later detained and taken to a hospital.
An AFP reporter at the scene saw ambulances and multiple police cars as personnel cordoned off the area — one of Poland’s landmark tourist hotspots popular with locals and foreign visitors.
“Everything suggests that the perpetrator held very, very radical views. A number of weapons were found in the car he was driving,” Kierwinski said.
“Everything suggests that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies” and held “ultra-nationalist views,” he added.
The man was wearing military-style clothing at the time of the attack, said Kierwinski.
Tusk praises ‘heroic’ police
Andrzej Fijolek, spokesman for the chief of police, said the attacker had used a semi-automatic rifle similar to the American AR-15.
The authorities have not yet disclosed the nationalities of all the victims of the attack, Poland’s deadliest shooting since the fall of communism in 1989.
“Our highest praise goes to the heroic police officers who risked their lives in the line of duty,” Tusk said.
On Saturday evening, AFP reporters saw the usually bustling Main Market Square sealed off, with heavily armed police and forensic investigators inspecting the site of the attack.
Witnesses told AFP they saw people take refuge in shops and restaurants in the surrounding streets.
“I saw a man shooting at people and walking around the square,” Annette, a woman in her sixties, told AFP.
“It’s a tragedy for Krakow, we’ve never seen anything like this before,” she added.

“I saw one person who was dead... and several others lying a bit farther away, whom people were still trying to resuscitate. They were taking off their clothes, trying to stem the blood with those clothes,” said musician Daniel Wolny, 32.
“It’s very frightening to think that there are still risks in Europe — risks of a terrorist nature,” Stella, a 22-year-old tourist from Rennes, northwest France, told AFP.

“Krakow has always been an extremely safe city... this is probably the first situation of this kind we can remember in our lifetime,” said 33-year-old Gabriel Bogdan, an employee at a bar near the square.
‘Dramatic events’
Deadly shootings are extremely rare in Poland, a European Union and Nato member of 38 million people.
But the country has been on high alert following a series of stabbings in October, which Tusk denounced as a “cult of violence”.
Warsaw, a staunch ally of Ukraine since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, has repeatedly warned of Russian sabotage and hybrid warfare on Polish soil, accusations rejected by Moscow.
Poland is also seeing a sharp rise in the number of firearms licences. In 2025, more than 50,000 new licences were issued, bringing the total to 411,000, according to police figures.
The historic city of Krakow in southern Poland was once the country’s capital and attracts millions of tourists every year.
In 2025, it was visited by 16.2 million people.
Poland’s conservative-nationalist president Karol Nawrocki said on X he was awaiting “a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these dramatic events”.
“The safety of Poles is an absolute priority,” he added.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky offered his condolences, saying that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with Poland and the Polish people. People have the right to safety.”
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on X that “Germany stands shoulder to shoulder with Poland as a friend and partner during these difficult times.”
The EU’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, described the shooting as “a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland”. — AFP
8a764844efe9630a: NEW YORK: Inter Miami's Lionel Messi became the first to win the MLS Golden Boot in back-to-back seasons, the league said on Saturday, the final day of the regular season.
Messi scored a league-high 26 goals across 31 matches, while FC Dallas forward Petar Musa followed with 22 goals and Nashville SC's Sam Surridge recorded 21.
He had 29 goals the previous season, becoming the second in league history to score at least 25 times in back-to-back years.
The 39-year-old Argentine retired from international football earlier this year after 21 years but signed a contract extension with the MLS club through 2028 in October.
The MLS Cup Playoffs begin on Nov 19. Inter Miami finished the regular season second in the Eastern Conference.

09b8e34145d5d423: LONDON, Nov 8 — A British monarch has only ever made one state visit to China: Queen Elizabeth II four decades ago. King Charles III would consider undertaking the second, according to an aide.
“If the government said, ‘Will the king go to China?’ I think, you know we think about it very carefully,” a senior palace aide told reporters this week.
The late queen, Charles’s mother, visited China with her husband Prince Philip in October 1986.
The trip included stops in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou, according to reports at the time.
It came two years after the signing of the Sino-British Joint Declaration setting out the terms for the return of Hong Kong, which improved relations between the two countries.
“This is the 40th anniversary of the last state visit,” noted the aide, speaking at the end of the king’s nine-day tour of the Caribbean.
Charles’s trip was dominated by the thorny subject of slavery reparations. He called the transatlantic slave trade a “monstrous injustice” as the UK government mulls an apology.
“I think what we’re seeing is a very clear pattern emerging of the government asking the king to head into quite politically charged situations, quite challenging situations,” said the aide.
The king, who is politically neutral, “relishes” the “tough parts” of his role and can be a “great secret weapon” for the government, the aide added.

“Whether that’s leading on the environment, whether it’s renewing and refreshing and reinvigorating relationships with nations where there have been some complex political issues at play, that is what he lives and breathes for,” they said.

Charles, who is nearly 78 and still being treated for an undisclosed cancer, was widely praised for his state visit to the United States and delicate handling of US President Donald Trump earlier this year.

Relations between London and Beijing have been strained for years, fuelled in part by tensions over the political situation in former British colony Hong Kong, criticism of Beijing’s human rights record and spying allegations.
But UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is now pursuing the same policy of cautious rapprochement started by his predecessor Keir Starmer, who visited Beijing in January.
“China is a hugely important country. It’s a very complex country. It would pose you know a lot of complexity in putting a programme together,” Charles’s aide said.
As then prince of Wales, Charles oversaw Hong Kong’s return to Chinese rule as Britain’s most senior representative at the 1997 handover alongside China’s then president Jiang Zemin.
Asked whether Burnham would be asking the king to visit China, his spokesman told AFP that questions about the monarch’s travel was “one for the palace”. — AFP
e3d02c34a0c0dd5b: DOHA, Nov 8 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil is scheduled to take part in two ministerial-level forums today focusing on strengthening international cooperation in the development and future of the digital ecosystem.

The two events are the Ministerial Panel at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026: Digital Leadership Forum and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) Ministerial Roundtable, both taking place at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Centre (DECC).
Fahmi’s participation in the two forums is among the key engagements of his working visit to Doha, where he is also leading the Malaysian delegation to ITU PP-26.

According to the official programme of the Malaysian delegation, Fahmi is scheduled to attend the MWC Doha 2026 welcome ceremony before joining a ministerial panel session titled “Accelerating Cooperation for a Connected Digital Future”.
The session will provide a platform for discussions on the importance of cooperation in shaping a more connected digital future.
In the afternoon, Fahmi is scheduled to attend the PP-26 Doha Ministerial Roundtable, which will feature opening remarks, ministerial presentations and a discussion session.
The programme will also see the launch of the Doha Ministerial Declaration, one of the key agenda items of the gathering.
Fahmi is also scheduled to visit exhibition booths operated by several international technology and telecommunications companies, including Huawei, Ericsson, Ooredoo, Nokia and VEON, at DECC.
In the evening, he is scheduled to attend a dinner hosted by the Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) in conjunction with MWC Doha.
Fahmi’s working visit to Doha also carries an important mission for Malaysia to retain its seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
ITU PP-26, held in Doha, is the organisation’s highest decision-making conference, convened every four years to determine its direction, policies and strategic plans.
Malaysia, which has been an ITU member since February 3, 1958, was elected to the ITU Council for the 2023-2026 term at the PP-22 conference in Bucharest, Romania. — Bernama
bd69beb2de6fc883: SANTIAGO, Nov 8 — After repelling eventual champions Spain and becoming an instant global celebrity, Vozinha was an unlikely hero of this year’s World Cup. But four months on from his tournament exploits, Cape Verde’s veteran goalkeeper is discovering that adapting to his new-found fame is not easy.
The 40-year-old, whose full name is Josimar Jose Evora Dias, moved to Chile in July and now finds himself struggling to settle at new club Colo Colo.

At the World Cup, Vozinha helped Cape Verde hold Spain to a 0-0 draw on their tournament debut as the tiny African island nation reached the last 32, where they took Lionel Messi’s Argentina to extra time before bowing out.
Before that game against Spain in Atlanta, Vozinha was just a journeyman goalkeeper who had spent his career shuffling between unremarkable clubs in Portugal, Cyprus and Slovakia.
A clean sheet against the World Cup favourites saw his Instagram account balloon from 50,000 followers to several million in a matter of hours. He now has 27.5 million followers.
Vozinha shed tears after that match, because of the scale of his and the team’s achievement, but also sadness at not being able to obtain a visa for his mother to be there.
After joining Colo Colo, Chile’s most successful side from the capital Santiago, he was unveiled at their Estadio Monumental before thousands of fans to a backdrop of fireworks.
He has been recruited by global brands like Adidas, Pepsi and Red Bull to be the face of advertising campaigns.
Vozinha also recently attended the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London as he came sixth in the voting for the the men’s goalkeeper of the year prize.
However, on the field the player who spent last season in Portugal’s second division has toiled.
By the start of November he had appeared in only five games out of a possible 14 for Colo Colo, who won the Copa Libertadores, South America’s equivalent of the Champions League, in 1991.
He was expected to be a substitute again this weekend, as his new team closes in on the Chilean title, and a place in next year’s Copa Libertadores.

“I came here with the intention of playing in the Libertadores, but my focus is on this week, which could be very important for Colo Colo. My future will be decided after that. I’m not thinking about that,” Vozinha told reporters.
Reluctant celebrity
Vozinha’s life was turned on its head following his World Cup exploits. He has moved to a new country, and went from being a virtual unknown to a celebrity with no privacy.
He worked as a rubbish collector before turning professional. To put his number of Instagram followers into perspective: the entire population of his native Cape Verde is only a little over 500,000.
“I’ve lost my peace and tranquillity,” Vozinha told British newspaper The Observer.

“I no longer have any privacy, or at least much less than I used to. Now I go out, I go to a restaurant, and there’s always someone who wants to take a photo with me or asks me for an autograph. Or, worse, someone is filming me.”
In the first few weeks after signing for Colo Colo, Vozinha regularly went to a bakery in the wealthy Vitacura neighbourhood of Santiago.
“I think it was good for him to go because he felt welcomed and was able to chat to people,” Gustavo Cassin, the manager of the cafe called Metissage, tells AFP.
Cassin and Vozinha avoided discussing football. The player would talk longingly about his home country as he waited for his morning croissant.
Will he stay?
The past, when he combined playing with teaching beach volleyball, is now a distant memory.
“To be honest, if I were offered the life I have today or the life I had before, I’d choose the one I had before,” he told The Observer.
In Chile, media are speculating as to whether Vozinha will remain into 2027 — he signed a six-month contract with Colo Colo extendable by a year only if he plays enough minutes.
He has faced criticism, with Chilean goalkeeping legend Claudio Bravo, formerly of Barcelona and Manchester City, questioning his ability.
“He has made several errors in situations that require coordination,” said the ex-Chile captain. “And if you don’t have coordination, you’ll never do it.”
Vozinha has a handful of games remaining before his contract runs out, and perhaps with it his Chilean adventure. — AFP
f026905f1951d591: ISTANBUL, Nov 8 — The Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) aims to double the number of sponsored students sent to pursue their studies in Turkiye next year, following the successful placement of its pioneer batch of 17 students in September.

Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the target was part of efforts to expand international education opportunities for outstanding students while strengthening academic ties between Malaysia and Turkiye.

“I will ensure that MARA sends at least twice as many students next year to the same universities, namely Sabanci University and Yildiz Technical University,” he said in a brief speech at a dinner with Malaysian students and staff of the Malaysian Embassy in Turkiye here on Saturday.
Also present were Deputy Foreign Affairs Ministry Secretary-General (Bilateral Affairs) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin and Malaysia’s Honorary Consul in Bursa, Turkiye, Datuk Cevdet Sefer.

Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said the students’ academic performance would be crucial in demonstrating that MARA had made the right choices in selecting them, thereby paving the way for more Malaysian students to benefit from similar opportunities in the future.

Ahmad Zahid, who also chairs the National Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Council, said Malaysian students pursuing their studies in Turkiye were not merely there to acquire knowledge but also served as young ambassadors of the country, reflecting Malaysia’s identity, character and image to the international community.

Meanwhile, MARA chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the placement of the first batch of students was successfully realised in September, just four months after discussions began, following Ahmad Zahid’s directive to expedite the initiative.
“They are among the best, selected from two MARA preparatory colleges after demonstrating outstanding academic performance since their Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examinations,” he said.

First-year Computer Science student at the Faculty of Science and Engineering, Sabanci University, Intan Alysha Safiya Hairil Alfian, 19, said MARA’s sponsorship had greatly helped meet her study expenses in Turkiye.

“MARA’s sponsorship has been a great help throughout our studies here, particularly the adequate living allowance, which is disbursed on time and makes things much easier for us as students living abroad,” she said when met at the event.

Meanwhile, first-year Mechatronics Engineering student at the Faculty of Engineering and Natural Sciences, Sabanci University, Haziq Firdaus Ramzizan, 20, said the MARA sponsorship allowed him to concentrate fully on his studies without being overly burdened by financial constraints.

Earlier in the day, MARA strengthened academic cooperation between Malaysia and Turkiye through the signing of Letters of Collaboration (LOCs) involving Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL) and Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia (UPTM), and Sabanci University and Yildiz Technical University (YTU).

d55db5cec6ed12ee: BANGKOK: Boasting K-pop and Bangladeshi beatboxing, Eurovision stages its first Asia edition this Saturday, bringing the European song contest's unique brand of kitsch and geopolitics to the world's most populous region.
From Laos to Mongolia and the Philippines, 11 countries are competing in the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok on Nov 14.
It will be broadcast live on television in participating countries and on YouTube -- but a question remains over whether anyone will be watching.
Eurovision is the world's biggest televised live music event, drawing 131 million viewers in 2026, and over the past 70 years has launched the careers of artists such as ABBA and Celine Dion.
The Asia edition is its first multinational expansion, although a US version was held in 2022 -- and was not repeated.
India, Japan and China are absent from the Bangkok event, while ticket sales have been sluggish.
"Eurovision is very big in Europe and it's very new in Asia," acknowledged executive producer Assaf Blecher.
But he said three years of preparations had fostered a public appetite for the show.
"Suddenly they understood the spirit of Eurovision," he said of those involved, hailing "the music, the extravagance".
"It's a window to other countries, to music, to people, to costumes," he told AFP, adding that he hoped it would be the first of many.
Some provocation
The finalists have been chosen through national competitions, some of them established stars such as Vietnam's Toc Tien, a favourite to win with her pop-dance track.
South Korea will be represented by K-pop star Junhee, Bangladesh is sending an all-male a cappella beatbox collective, Beatmosphere, while Pratik Himal Rai is rocking it out for Nepal.
The Asia edition comes as Eurovision marks its 70th birthday under a cloud, with 2026 viewing figures down 35 million on the year after a boycott by five countries over Israel's participation.
But the contest has always been marked by controversy, from protests in the 1960s over the participation of Franco-ruled Spain to Russia's exclusion over the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

The show was first held in 1956 as an experiment by national public broadcasters and became a cultural phenomenon, known for its over-the-top staging, kitsch and eclectic music, and with a large LGBTQ following.
It grew as Europe became more integrated -- although its reach exceeds the continent's borders, with Canada joining next year -- and became as much about the politics as the music.
Votes are gathered by participating country, half from a jury and half from viewers, and no nation can vote for itself -- meaning ballots are often cast based on national relationships.
In the Asia contest, this could see viewers from Cambodia and Thailand, who clashed over their border last year, voting against each other, Blecher noted.
But the entries to Eurovision Asia -- which unlike the original is organised by commercial broadcasters -- are mostly love songs, lamented Dean Vuletic, an author and expert on Eurovision.
He noted as an exception Philippines pop singer Carmelle, whose "Sobra-Sobra" (Too Much) is an upbeat call to female empowerment.
The show is "lacking some provocation or some meaningful messaging that can resonate with international audiences", Vuletic told AFP.
"This is what makes Eurovision in Europe special from other song contests."
Budget cuts
The show has been hit by production issues, including a reported budget cut of one million dollars, forcing organisers to issue a statement last month insisting it was going ahead.
"There are always issues with budgets," Blecher insisted.
"This is the first year and we're working with some limitations," he said, adding that it would be a "beautiful production".
The performers were due to arrive this weekend in Bangkok ahead of rehearsals for the final show.
Some will sing in their native language, others in English, a choice made by Malaysian star Aina Abdul to reach a wider audience.
For Bhutan's Nyendra, who is performing his folk-pop love song in traditional dress, the show offers a platform well beyond his country of 800,000 inhabitants.
And he could do well, as Eurovision viewers have a habit of supporting the smallest countries, the underdogs.
Blecher says he already has 16 or 17 places interested in a 2027 edition, if all goes well this week.
He cites China, Hong Kong and Taiwan among those interested -- a selection that would certainly put the contest on the geopolitical map.

6ea945f382f18776: From Ibrahim M Ahmad
The dispute over former prime minister Najib Razak’s proposed transfer from Kajang Prison to house arrest is no longer simply about whether he should go home.

At its core, the controversy raises a broader question: what happens when a royal pardon, a court order and a separate criminal sentence intersect in ways that existing laws do not clearly anticipate?

The latest developments have placed the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC), the prisons department, Najib’s lawyers and even Istana Negara on seemingly different sides of a debate over implementation rather than principle. All parties say they are attempting to uphold the law. The disagreement is over what the law, and the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's decree, require in practice.
That distinction is important.

Public discussion has largely centred on whether Najib should be released from prison immediately. Yet the more significant issue may be whether Malaysia’s legal framework adequately addresses a situation in which a prisoner is granted a conditional royal pardon while also facing another custodial sentence.

The King’s position appears straightforward. Najib was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest, provided he paid the RM50 million fine imposed by the court. That condition has now been met.
Ordinarily, that would appear to settle the matter.

However, the High Court document issued following payment of the fine has introduced uncertainty over the legal effect of Najib’s "discharge" and whether the SRC sentence continues to run until 2028 or is regarded as completed.

The document, called an “Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine”, directs that Najib be discharged immediately. But it also states that the remainder of his sentence is to be served under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.

The question is what “discharged” means in this context. Does it mean he should leave Kajang Prison and continue serving his SRC sentence at home? Or could it mean that the SRC sentence is legally complete? The AGC says clarification is needed on the effect of the order.
The distinction is far from academic.

Najib’s separate 15-year prison sentence in the 1MDB case was ordered to begin only after the SRC sentence ends. If the SRC sentence continues under house arrest, the chronology is uncomplicated. If it is deemed complete upon payment of the fine, questions arise about whether the 1MDB sentence should begin immediately.
Faced with that uncertainty, the AGC argues that clarification is needed before any transfer takes place.

Critics may see this as an unnecessary delay, particularly after Istana Negara stated that all conditions of the pardon had been fulfilled. Supporters of the AGC’s position, however, contend that resolving ambiguity now is preferable to triggering fresh legal challenges later.
Neither argument is entirely without merit.

What the episode has exposed is a potential gap in Malaysia’s legal architecture. While imprisonment, parole and remission are governed by established laws and procedures, house arrest remains relatively unfamiliar territory. There is no comprehensive statutory framework setting out how such arrangements should operate, how compliance should be monitored or how they interact with other criminal sentences.
That absence has created room for competing interpretations.

The issue also extends beyond Najib himself. Any legal principles established in his case could influence how future pardons are implemented and how exceptional forms of custody are administered. For that reason, the courts’ eventual interpretation may carry implications beyond one high-profile prisoner.
At the same time, there is a public confidence dimension that cannot be ignored.

Najib’s status as a former prime minister means every development is scrutinised through the lens of equality before the law. Many Malaysians will want assurance that whatever outcome emerges is grounded in clear legal principles rather than political considerations or institutional pressure.
That makes transparency critical.
The public deserves a clear explanation of how the pardon is meant to operate, how the prison and court orders interact, and how the separate 1MDB sentence fits into the equation.

Ultimately, the dispute should not become a contest between institutions. The King’s decree, the courts and the executive branch each have defined constitutional roles. The challenge lies in ensuring those roles operate coherently when they overlap.

The immediate question is whether Najib leaves prison or remains there for the time being. The more enduring question is whether Malaysia’s legal system can provide a clear and consistent answer when faced with circumstances that its laws did not expressly anticipate.
That is an issue that extends well beyond Najib Razak.
Ibrahim M Ahmad is an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
